sentences.zh: 賈充，字公閭，平陽襄陵人也。

translations.literal: Jia Chong, courtesy name Gonglü, was a man of Xiangling in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong, whose courtesy name was Gonglü, came from Xiangling in Pingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父逵，魏豫州刺史、陽里亭侯。

translations.literal: His father Jia Kui was Inspector of Yu Province under Wei and village marquis of Yangli ting.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Jia Kui, had served Wei as inspector of Yu Province and held the village marquisate of Yangli.

sentences.zh: 逵晚始生充，言後當有充閭之慶，故以為名字焉。

translations.literal: Kui was advanced in years when Chong was born; he said that later there would be the auspicious sign of 'filling the gate,' and therefore made this his name and courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui was already old when Chong was born; he declared that the family would one day know the omen of a child who would "fill the gate" with renown, and so he chose Chong's name and courtesy name accordingly.

sentences.zh: 充少孤，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Chong was orphaned young; in mourning he was heard of for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Chong lost his father while still young and earned a reputation for filial devotion during the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵為侯。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's noble rank and became a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to his father's marquisate.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書郎，典定科令，兼度支考課。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, supervised the fixing of statutes and ordinances, and concurrently handled fiscal audit and personnel evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed gentleman clerk at the Masters of Writing, where he oversaw the drafting of statutes and regulations and also managed fiscal reviews and performance assessments.

sentences.zh: 辯章節度，事皆施用。

translations.literal: He distinguished and regulated measures and procedures; in affairs everything was applied.
translations.idiomatic: He clarified procedures and balanced priorities so that every measure could actually be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 累遷黃門侍郎、汲郡典農中郎將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and Commandant of Agriculture of Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates and commandant of agriculture for Ji commandery.

sentences.zh: 參大將軍軍事，從景帝討毌丘儉、文欽于樂嘉。

translations.literal: He participated in the Grand General's military affairs and followed Emperor Jing to campaign against Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin at Lejia.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the staff of the grand general and accompanied Emperor Jing on the campaign against Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin at Lejia.

sentences.zh: 帝疾篤，還許昌，留充監諸軍事，以勞增邑三百五十戶。

translations.literal: The Emperor was gravely ill and returned to Xuchang; he left Chong to supervise all military affairs; for his merit his fief was increased by three hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor grew desperately ill and withdrew to Xuchang, he left Jia Chong to oversee military operations; for this service another three hundred fifty households were added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 後為文帝大將軍司馬，轉右長史。

translations.literal: Later he became marshal to the Grand General under Emperor Wen and was transferred to senior administrator on the right.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Emperor Wen as marshal to the grand general, then moved to the post of senior administrator on the right.

sentences.zh: 帝新執朝權，恐方鎮有異議，使充詣諸葛誕，圖欲伐吳，陰察其變。

translations.literal: The Emperor had newly grasped court power and feared that regional commanders might dissent; he sent Chong to Zhuge Dan, ostensibly planning to attack Wu but secretly observing Dan's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just seized control at court and worried that frontier commanders might object; he dispatched Jia Chong to Zhuge Dan under the pretense of planning a campaign against Wu while secretly sounding out Dan's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 充既論說時事，因謂誕曰：「天下皆願禪代，君以為如何？

translations.literal: After Chong had discussed current affairs, he therefore said to Dan, "All under Heaven wish for abdication and replacement; what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Once they had finished reviewing the political situation, Chong said to Zhuge Dan, "Everyone expects the throne to change hands; what is your view?

sentences.zh: 」誕曆聲曰：「卿非賈豫州子乎，世受魏恩，豈可欲以社稷輸人乎！

translations.literal: " Dan raised his voice and said, "Are you not the son of Inspector Jia of Yu? Generation after generation you have received Wei's grace—how can you wish to hand the altars of soil and grain to someone else!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuge Dan answered sharply, "You are the son of Jia Kui of Yu Province; your family has enjoyed Wei's favor for generations—how dare you speak of handing the realm to another!

sentences.zh: 若洛中有難，吾當死之。

translations.literal: If there is trouble in Luoyang, I shall die for it.
translations.idiomatic: If Luoyang faces peril, I will die defending it.

sentences.zh: 」充默然。

translations.literal: " Chong was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Jia Chong said nothing.

sentences.zh: 及還，白帝曰：「誕在再揚州，威名夙著，能得人死力。

translations.literal: When he returned, he reported to the Emperor, saying, "Dan is again in Yangzhou; his martial reputation is long established; he can obtain from men devoted effort unto death.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he told the emperor, "Zhuge Dan is back in Yangzhou; his prestige is long-standing, and men will fight to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 觀其規略，為反必也。

translations.literal: Observing his planning and strategy, he will surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Judging from his designs, rebellion is only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 今征之，反速而事小；

translations.literal: Now if we summon him, his rebellion will be swift but the affair small;
translations.idiomatic: Summon him now and he will rebel quickly, yet the crisis stays manageable;

sentences.zh: 不征，事遲而禍大。

translations.literal: if we do not summon him, the affair will be delayed but the calamity great.
translations.idiomatic: leave him be and trouble comes later, but the disaster will be far worse.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃征誕為司空，而誕果叛。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon summoned Dan to be Minister of Works, and Dan indeed rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accordingly summoned Zhuge Dan to the capital as minister of works, and Dan rose in rebellion as predicted.

sentences.zh: 復從征誕，充進計曰：「楚兵輕而銳，若深溝高壘以逼賊城，可不戰而克也。

translations.literal: Again following the campaign against Dan, Chong advanced a plan, saying, "The Chu troops are light and keen; if we dig deep moats and raise high ramparts to press the rebel city, we can take it without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched again against Zhuge Dan, Chong urged a strategy: "The enemy from Chu country is mobile and aggressive; starve them out with deep trenches and high walls against their fort and you win without a pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 城陷，帝登壘以勞充。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the Emperor mounted the ramparts to commend Chong.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, the emperor climbed the siege works to commend Jia Chong before the army.

sentences.zh: 帝先歸洛陽，使充統後事，進爵宣陽鄉侯，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: The Emperor first returned to Luoyang and ordered Chong to oversee subsequent affairs; his noble rank was advanced to village marquis of Xuanyang and his fief increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode back to Luoyang first and left Chong to manage the rear echelon; Chong was promoted to village marquis of Xuanyang with another thousand households added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 遷廷尉，充雅長法理，有平反之稱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commandant of Justice; Chong was elegant and adept at legal principles and had a reputation for overturning wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to commandant of justice, Chong excelled at statutory reasoning and earned praise for correcting unjust verdicts.

sentences.zh: 轉中護軍，高貴鄉公之攻相府也，充率眾距戰于南闕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Central Protector of the Army; when the Duke of Gaoguixiang attacked the Chancellor's compound, Chong led troops to resist battle at the southern gate-tower.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to central protector of the army, Chong led troops against the duke of Gaoguixiang when that puppet emperor assaulted the grand chancellor's headquarters, fighting at the southern portal.

sentences.zh: 軍將敗，騎督成倅弟太子舍人濟謂充曰：「今日之事如何？

translations.literal: The army was about to be defeated; the younger brother of Cavalry Commander Cheng Cui, Attendant to the Heir Apparent Cheng Ji, said to Chong, "How shall matters stand today?
translations.idiomatic: As the lines began to buckle, Cheng Ji—commandant of cavalry Cheng Cui's brother and an attendant at the heir apparent's residence—asked Chong, "What are we to do now?

sentences.zh: 」充曰：「公等養汝，正擬今日，復何疑！

translations.literal: " Chong said, "The Duke and company raised you precisely for today—why further doubt!
translations.idiomatic: " Chong replied, "Your masters kept you fed for exactly this moment—what more is there to hesitate over?

sentences.zh: 」濟於是抽戈犯蹕。

translations.literal: " Ji thereupon drew his halberd and violated the imperial escort.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng Ji then drew his spear and struck at the emperor's guard.

sentences.zh: 及常道鄉公即位，進封安陽鄉侯，增邑千二百戶，統城外諸軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Changdao village assumed the throne, Chong's fief was advanced to village marquis of Anyang with an increase of one thousand two hundred households; he commanded all troops outside the walls and was additionally appointed Regular Cavalry Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the duke of Changdao village mounted the throne, Chong was promoted to village marquis of Anyang with twelve hundred more households, took charge of the armies beyond the capital walls, and received the concurrent title of regular attendant at cavalry.

sentences.zh: 鐘會謀反於蜀，帝假充節，以本官都督關中、隴右諸軍事，西據漢中，未至而會死。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui plotted rebellion in Shu; the Emperor lent Chong credentials of authority and, in his existing office, put him in charge of all military affairs of Guanzhong and Longyou, advancing west to hold Hanzhong; before he arrived, Hui died.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui rebelled in Shu, the emperor gave Chong the imperial baton and, while retaining his current rank, placed him in overall command of Guanzhong and Longyou and sent him west toward Hanzhong—Zhong Hui died before Chong arrived.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多事，朝廷機密，皆與籌之。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were numerous; court secrets were all planned with him.
translations.idiomatic: With warfare and administration both demanding constant attention, the throne consulted Chong on every sensitive decision.

sentences.zh: 帝甚信重充，與裴秀、王沈、羊祜、荀勖同受腹心之任。

translations.literal: The Emperor trusted and esteemed Chong greatly; together with Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, Yang Hu, and Xun Xu he received duties of the innermost heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relied deeply on Chong and assigned him, along with Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, Yang Hu, and Xun Xu, to the emperor's inner circle of confidential advisers.

sentences.zh: 帝又命充定法律。

translations.literal: The Emperor also ordered Chong to fix the laws.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor further charged him with codifying the legal statutes.

sentences.zh: 假金章，賜甲第一區。

translations.literal: He was lent a gold seal and granted one precinct of armored residences.
translations.idiomatic: He received temporary use of the gold seal of office and was awarded a walled mansion of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 五等初建，封臨沂侯，為晉元勳，深見寵異，祿賜常優於群官。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were first established, he was enfeoffed as marquis of Linyi; as a founding merit minister of Jin he was deeply favored and distinguished; salary and gifts were constantly superior to those of other officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the five-tier nobility was instituted he became marquis of Linyi; as one of Jin's founding pillars he enjoyed extraordinary favor, with stipends and gifts routinely exceeding those of his peers.

sentences.zh: 充有刀筆才，能觀察上旨。

translations.literal: Chong had administrative drafting talent and could observe and discern the superior's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had a clerk's sharp pen and an instinct for reading his sovereign's wishes.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝以景帝恢贊王業，方傳位於舞陽侯攸。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wen, because Emperor Jing had broadly aided the royal enterprise, was about to transmit the position to Marquis Wu of Wuyang, Sima You.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Wen believed Emperor Jing had done most to enlarge the Sima enterprise and planned to pass the succession to Sima You, marquis of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 充稱武帝寬仁，且又居長，有人君之德，宜奉社稷。

translations.literal: Chong declared that Emperor Wu was generous and humane, and moreover occupied the senior position; he had the virtue of a lord of men and ought to receive the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Chong argued that Emperor Wu—Sima Yan—was magnanimous by nature, the eldest son, and possessed true monarchical virtue, and therefore should inherit the realm.

sentences.zh: 及文帝寢疾，武帝請問後事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen lay ill abed, Emperor Wu asked about subsequent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took to his sickbed, Sima Yan sought guidance on what would follow.

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「知汝者賈公閭也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said, "The one who understands you is Jia Gonglü.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen answered, "Jia Gonglü is the man who knows your worth.

sentences.zh: 」帝襲王位，拜充晉國衛將軍、儀同三司、給事中，改封臨潁侯。

translations.literal: " The Emperor inherited the royal throne and appointed Chong General Who Guards the Army of the Jin state, with parity of ceremony to the Three Offices, and Concurrent Palace Attendant; his fief was changed to marquis of Linying.
translations.idiomatic: " After Sima Yan assumed the princely throne he named Chong general who guards the armies of the Jin principality with Three Offices protocol and concurrent palace attendant, and transferred his title to marquis of Linying.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，充以建明大命，轉車騎將軍、散騎常侍、尚書僕射，更封魯郡公，母柳氏為魯國太夫人。

translations.literal: When the abdication was received, Chong for clarifying and manifesting the great mandate was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Regular Cavalry Attendant, and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; he was further enfeoffed as duke of Lu commandery, and his mother Lady Liu became Grand Lady of the Lu state.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei yielded the throne, Chong—honored for proclaiming the new mandate—became general of chariots and cavalry, regular cavalry attendant, and vice director of the Masters of Writing; he was raised to duke of Lu, and his mother, Lady Liu, received the title of grand lady of Lu.

sentences.zh: 充所定新律既班于天下，百姓便之。

translations.literal: The new statutes that Chong had fixed having already been promulgated throughout the realm, the hundred surnames found them convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Once the new code Chong had drafted went into force across the empire, ordinary people found it easier to live under.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「漢氏以來，法令嚴峻。

translations.literal: An edict stated, "Since the Han house, statutes and ordinances have been harsh and severe.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "From Han times onward the laws had grown harsh and intricate.

sentences.zh: 故自元成之世，及建安、嘉平之間，咸欲辯章舊典，刪革刑書。

translations.literal: Therefore from the eras of Yuan and Cheng down to the interval between Jian'an and Jiaping, all wished to distinguish and clarify old canons and delete and reform penal writings.
translations.idiomatic: So from the reigns of Yuan and Cheng through the Jian'an and Jiaping periods, successive courts tried to rationalize ancient precedent and streamline the criminal code.

sentences.zh: 述作體大，歷年無成。

translations.literal: The undertaking was vast in scope; through years nothing was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The project was enormous, and year after year it remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 先帝湣元元之命陷於密網，親發德音，厘正名實。

translations.literal: The former Emperor pitied the fate of the primal masses trapped in dense nets; personally he issued virtuous pronouncements to rectify names and realities.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor lamented how common folk were caught in a tangled web of statutes and himself issued humane orders to align law with justice.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍賈充，獎明聖意，諮詢善道。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong encouraged and clarified sage intentions and consulted on good methods.
translations.idiomatic: General of chariots and cavalry Jia Chong carried forward the sovereign's intent and guided deliberation on sound legal principles.

sentences.zh: 太傅鄭沖，又與司空荀顗、中書監荀勖、中軍將軍羊祜、中護軍王業，及廷尉杜友、守河南尹杜預、散騎侍郎裴楷、潁川太守周雄、齊相郭頎、騎都尉成公綏荀煇、尚書郎柳軌等，典正其事。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, together with Minister of Works Xun Yi, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Xun Xu, General of the Central Army Yang Hu, Central Protector of the Army Wang Ye, Commandant of Justice Du You, Acting Governor of Henan Du Yu, Gentleman Cavalier Attendant Pei Kai, Administrator of Yingchuan Zhou Xiong, Chancellor of Qi Guo Qi, Commandants of Cavalry Cheng Gongsui and Xun Hui, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Liu Gui, and others, supervised and corrected the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Zheng Chong joined Ministers Xun Yi and Xun Xu, Generals Yang Hu and Wang Ye, the commandants Du You and Du Yu, attendant Pei Kai, regional officials Zhou Xiong and Guo Qi, cavalry commandants Cheng Gongsui and Xun Hui, clerk Liu Gui, and their colleagues in supervising the revision.

sentences.zh: 朕每鑒其用心，常慨然嘉之。

translations.literal: We have constantly mirrored their intentions of heart and always sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever We observed their dedication, Our admiration deepened.

sentences.zh: 今法律既成，始班天下，刑寬禁簡，足以克當先旨。

translations.literal: Now the laws are completed and first promulgated throughout the realm; punishments are lenient and prohibitions simplified, sufficient to match the prior intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the code is finished and published empire-wide, punishments are moderate and statutes succinct—exactly what Our predecessors intended.

sentences.zh: 昔蕭何以定律受封，叔孫通以制儀為奉常，賜金五百斤，弟子皆為郎。

translations.literal: Formerly Xiao He received enfeoffment for fixing statutes; Shu Sun Tong for framing ceremonies became Chamberlain of Ceremonials and was gifted five hundred jin of gold; his disciples all became gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Xiao He earned his marquisate by drafting Han law; Shu Sun Tong rose to chamberlain of ceremonies for designing court ritual and received five hundred jin of gold while his students became palace gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 夫立功立事，古之所重。

translations.literal: Establishing merit and accomplishing affairs is what antiquity esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Merit earned through service has always been honored.

sentences.zh: 自太傅、車騎以下，皆加祿賞。

translations.literal: From the Grand Tutor and General of Chariots and Cavalry downward, all receive increased salary and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone from the grand tutor and General Jia Chong downward shall receive augmented stipends and gifts.

sentences.zh: 其詳依故典。

translations.literal: Let the details follow former canons.
translations.idiomatic: Specific grants shall follow established precedent.

sentences.zh: 」於是賜充子弟一人關內侯，絹五百匹。

translations.literal: " Thereupon one of Chong's sons or younger brothers was gifted village marquis within the passes, and five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " One of Chong's junior kinsmen was enfeoffed as secondary marquis within the passes, and five hundred bolts of silk were awarded.

sentences.zh: 固讓，不許。

translations.literal: He firmly declined; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He protested repeatedly but the throne would not hear of refusal.

sentences.zh: 後代裴秀為尚書令，常侍、車騎將軍如故。

translations.literal: Later he succeeded Pei Xiu as Director of the Masters of Writing; Regular Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He later succeeded Pei Xiu as director of the Masters of Writing while keeping his posts as regular attendant and general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋改常侍為侍中，賜絹七百匹。

translations.literal: Soon Regular Attendant was changed to Palace Attendant; seven hundred bolts of silk were gifted.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward his title was upgraded from regular attendant to palace attendant, with a gift of seven hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，詔遣黃門侍郎慰問。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his mother he left office; an edict dispatched a Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates to console him.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother, and the court sent a gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates with condolences.

sentences.zh: 又以東南有事，遣典軍將軍楊囂宣諭，使六旬還內。

translations.literal: Also because there were affairs in the southeast, Camp General Yang Xiao was dispatched to proclaim instructions, ordering him to return inside within sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: Because campaigns were underway in the southeast, camp general Yang Xiao brought word that Chong must resume duty within sixty days.

sentences.zh: 充為政，務農節用，並官省職，帝善之，又以文武異容，求罷所領兵。

translations.literal: In administering governance Chong strove for farming and economizing use, merging offices and eliminating posts; the Emperor approved of this; also because civil and military presentation differed, he sought to dismiss the troops he commanded.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he stressed agriculture and frugality, merging redundant offices; the emperor praised him, and Chong—claiming civil and military roles ill suited one another—asked to surrender command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 及羊祜等出鎮，充復上表欲立勳邊境，帝並不許。

translations.literal: When Yang Hu and others went out to garrison the frontiers, Chong again submitted memorials wishing to establish merit on the borders; the Emperor alike did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Hu and others took frontier commands, Chong repeatedly volunteered for border duty to earn glory; each time the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 從容任職，褒貶在已，頗好進士，每有所薦達，必終始經緯之，是以士多歸焉。

translations.literal: At ease in holding office, praise and blame lay with himself; he quite favored advancing gentlemen; whenever he had someone recommended and promoted, he invariably began and completed weaving support for them; therefore gentlemen largely attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed comfortable at court, controlling reputations as he pleased. He liked cultivating protégés; whenever he sponsored someone he followed that man's career from start to finish, so scholars flocked to his faction.

sentences.zh: 帝舅王恂嘗毀充，而充更進恂。

translations.literal: The Emperor's maternal uncle Wang Xun once slandered Chong, yet Chong further advanced Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's uncle Wang Xun had spoken ill of Chong, yet Chong arranged further promotions for him.

sentences.zh: 或有背充以要權貴者，充皆陽以素意待之。

translations.literal: Some who turned against Chong to seek powerful nobles, Chong all outwardly treated them with his customary intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Those who betrayed him to curry favor with grandees still found Chong greeting them with pretended goodwill.

sentences.zh: 而充無公方之操，不能正身率下，專以諂媚取容。

translations.literal: Yet Chong lacked the conduct of public rectitude; unable to correct himself and lead subordinates, he relied solely on flattery to obtain acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chong lacked upright principle; he could not set an example for subordinates and relied on flattery alone to stay in favor.

sentences.zh: 侍中任愷、中書令庾純等剛直守正，咸共疾之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Ren Kai, Director of the Secretariat Yu Chun, and others were rigidly upright and guarded correctness; together they all despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Ren Kai and director Yu Chun—men of stubborn integrity—joined others in detesting him.

sentences.zh: 又以充女為齊王妃，懼後益盛。

translations.literal: Moreover because Chong's daughter became Princess Consort of Qi, they feared that afterward he would become ever more powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's daughter had married the prince of Qi as his consort, stoking fears that his clan would grow unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 及氐羌反叛，時帝深以為慮，愷因進說，請充鎮關中。

translations.literal: When the Di and Qiang rebelled, at that time the Emperor deeply took it as a worry; Kai therefore advanced persuasion, requesting that Chong garrison Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Di and Qiang tribes rose in revolt, the emperor grew anxious; Ren Kai seized the moment and urged that Chong be posted to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「秦涼二境，比年屢敗，胡虜縱暴，百姓荼毒。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued, stating, "The two regions of Qin and Liang, in successive years have repeatedly been defeated; barbarian captives run rampant; the hundred surnames suffer poison.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Qin and Liang have suffered defeat after defeat; nomads raid at will while common people endure misery.

sentences.zh: 遂使異類扇動，害及中州。

translations.literal: Thereupon causing alien kinds to stir and move; harm reaches the central provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Alien peoples stir rebellion and their violence spills into the heartland.

sentences.zh: 雖復吳蜀之寇，未嘗至此。

translations.literal: Although again Wu and Shu's marauders, never reached here.
translations.idiomatic: Even the devastations wrought by Wu and Shu never grew this dire.

sentences.zh: 誠由所任不足以內撫夷夏，外鎮醜逆，輕用其眾而不能盡其力。

translations.literal: Truly it is because those appointed are insufficient to inwardly soothe barbarians and Chinese, outwardly suppress ugly rebels; lightly employing their masses yet unable to exhaust their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The fault lies with ill-chosen commanders who neither pacify tribes and Han settlers within nor crush rebels beyond, wasting armies without bringing their full strength to bear.

sentences.zh: 非得腹心之重，推轂委成，大匡其弊，恐為患未已。

translations.literal: Unless one obtains the weight of an inner-heart minister, pushes the carriage shaft and entrusts accomplishment, greatly correcting its flaws, I fear the calamity will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Without a trusted minister empowered to lead wholeheartedly and set these failures right, the crisis will not end.

sentences.zh: 每慮斯難，忘寢與食。

translations.literal: Whenever considering this difficulty, forgetting sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: These worries rob Us of sleep and appetite.

sentences.zh: 侍中、守尚書令、車騎將軍賈充，雅量弘高，達見明遠，武有折沖之威，文懷經國之慮，信結人心，名震域外。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, Acting Director of the Masters of Writing, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong has elegant capacity broadly lofty; penetrating insight bright and far-reaching; in martial matters possesses the might to blunt enemies; in civil affairs cherishes planning for ordering the state; trust binds men's hearts; his name shakes beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant, acting director of the Masters of Writing, and general of chariots and cavalry Jia Chong combines breadth of mind with foresight—bold enough to overawe foes in war, thoughtful enough to steward the realm in peace—winning devotion at home and renown abroad.

sentences.zh: 使權統方任，綏靜西夏，則吾無西顧之念，而遠近獲安矣。

translations.literal: Let him be entrusted with regional responsibility to pacify and quiet the western Xia; then We shall have no thought of looking west, and far and near obtain peace.
translations.idiomatic: Invest him with frontier command to pacify the western reaches and We need no longer glance anxiously toward the west; border and interior alike will rest easier.

sentences.zh: 其以充為使持節、都督秦涼二州諸軍事，侍中、車騎將軍如故，假羽葆、鼓吹，給第一駙馬。

translations.literal: Let Chong be Bearer of Credentials, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of Qin and Liang provinces; Palace Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry as before; lent feather-canopy and drum-and-pipe; supplied first-grade auxiliary horse.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint Chong credential-bearing commander of Qin and Liang with his existing titles retained; grant him feather canopy, martial music, and the finest mount from the imperial stable.

sentences.zh: 」朝之賢良欲進忠規獻替者，皆幸充此舉，望隆惟新之化。

translations.literal: " Those worthy and good at court who wished to advance loyal counsel and offer replacements all rejoiced at Chong's undertaking this action, hoping for abundant renewal transformation.
translations.idiomatic: " Court reformers who hoped to speak frankly welcomed this posting, expecting it to herald broader renewal.

sentences.zh: 充既外出，自以為失職，深銜任愷，計無所從。

translations.literal: Chong having gone forth outward, himself considered that he had lost his duty and deeply harbored resentment toward Ren Kai; stratagem had nowhere from which to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Banishment westward felt like loss of power to Chong; he nursed a bitter grudge against Ren Kai yet saw no way to strike back.

sentences.zh: 將之鎮，百僚餞於夕陽亭，荀勖私焉。

translations.literal: About to depart to his garrison, the hundred officials saw him off at Sunset Pavilion; Xun Xu spoke with him privately.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to leave for his command, courtiers gathered at Sunset Pavilion to bid farewell; Xun Xu drew him aside.

sentences.zh: 充以憂告，勖曰：「公，國之宰輔，而為一夫所制，不亦鄙乎！

translations.literal: Chong reported his anxiety; Xu said, "Lord, you are the state's chief minister, yet are controlled by one man—is it not base!
translations.idiomatic: Chong poured out his worries; Xu replied, "You lead the realm yet let one man dictate your fate—how unworthy!

sentences.zh: 然是行也，辭之實難，獨有結婚太子，不頓駕而自留矣。

translations.literal: Yet this undertaking, declining it is truly difficult; only by marrying into the heir apparent need you not halt your carriage yet naturally remain.
translations.idiomatic: Refusing the posting outright is impossible; marry your daughter to the heir apparent and you never need mount the carriage west—you stay in Luoyang by royal marriage.

sentences.zh: 」充曰：「然。

translations.literal: " Chong said, "So.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong said, "You're right.

sentences.zh: 孰可寄懷？

translations.literal: To whom may I entrust my intention?
translations.idiomatic: Who will carry this out?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「勖請行之。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Xu requests to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu answered, "Leave it to me.

sentences.zh: 」俄而侍宴，論太子婚姻事，勖因言充女才質令淑，宜配儲宮。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward attending a banquet, discussing the heir apparent's marriage affairs, Xu thereupon stated that Chong's daughter's talents and qualities were admirable and virtuous, fitting to match the heir's palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward at a palace banquet the conversation turned to the heir's marriage; Xu praised Chong's daughter as refined and virtuous—ideal for the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 而楊皇后及荀顗亦並稱之。

translations.literal: And Empress Yang and Xun Yi also together praised her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang and Xun Yi echoed his endorsement.

sentences.zh: 帝納其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted their words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 會京師大雪，平地二尺，軍不得發。

translations.literal: It happened that in the capital region great snow fell, two chi deep on level ground; the army could not set out.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow then blanketed the capital two feet deep, blocking any march west.

sentences.zh: 既而皇儲當婚，遂不西行。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the imperial heir was about to marry; therefore he did not travel west.
translations.idiomatic: Once the heir's nuptials were arranged, Chong never went west after all.

sentences.zh: 詔充居本職。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chong to remain in his original posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commanded Chong to stay at his current duties in the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是羊祜密啟留充，及是，帝以語充。

translations.literal: Earlier Yang Hu had secretly memorialized to retain Chong; when it came to this, the Emperor informed Chong of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu had privately urged the throne to keep Chong in Luoyang; now the emperor told Chong what Hu had done.

sentences.zh: 充謝祜曰：「始知君長者。」

translations.literal: Chong thanked Hu, saying, "Only now do I know you are an elder worthy."
translations.idiomatic: Chong thanked him: "Now I see what a generous patron you are."

sentences.zh: 時吳將孫秀降，拜為驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: At that time Wu general Sun Xiu surrendered and was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu, a Wu commander who had defected, had just been named grand general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 帝以充舊臣。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered Chong an old minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to honor Chong as a veteran of his house.

sentences.zh: 欲改班，使車騎居驃騎之右。

translations.literal: He wished to revise court ranking so that General of Chariots and Cavalry should stand to the right of Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed reshuffling precedence so that general of chariots and cavalry would rank above grand general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 充固讓，見聽。

translations.literal: Chong firmly declined; his view was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Chong protested until the emperor dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 尋遷司空，侍中、尚書令、領兵如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Minister of Works; Palace Attendant, Director of the Masters of Writing, and command of troops remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to minister of works while keeping his posts as palace attendant, director of the Masters of Writing, and troop command.

sentences.zh: 會帝寢疾，充及齊王攸、荀勖參醫藥。

translations.literal: When the Emperor lay ill abed, Chong together with Prince of Qi You and Xun Xu participated in medicines.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell seriously ill, Chong joined Prince Sima You of Qi and Xun Xu in supervising his medical care.

sentences.zh: 及疾愈，賜絹各五百匹。

translations.literal: When he recovered from illness, each was gifted five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor recovered, each of them received five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 初，帝疾篤，朝廷屬意於攸。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor was gravely ill, the court looked toward You.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the emperor's grave illness, court opinion favored Sima You as successor.

sentences.zh: 河南尹夏侯和謂充曰：「卿二女婿，親疏等耳，立人當立德。

translations.literal: Governor of Henan Xiahou He said to Chong, "Your two sons-in-law are equal in closeness and distance; when establishing a person one ought to establish virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou He, governor of Henan, told Chong, "Your two royal sons-in-law stand equally close as kin—choose the heir by moral worth."

sentences.zh: 」充不答。

translations.literal: " Chong did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong kept silent.

sentences.zh: 及是，帝聞之，徙和光祿勳，乃奪充兵權，而位遇無替。

translations.literal: When it came to this, the Emperor heard of it and transferred He to Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison; thereupon he stripped Chong of military authority, yet rank and treatment were not replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this exchange, the emperor transferred Xiahou He to chamberlain of the palace garrison and stripped Chong of military command while leaving his civil honors untouched.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太尉、行太子太保、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Grand Commandant, conducting affairs of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and recording Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand commandant, acting junior tutor to the heir apparent, with overall charge of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 咸寧三年，日蝕於三朝，充請遜位，不許。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianning, there was a solar eclipse at the Three Courts; Chong requested to yield position; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianning 3 a solar eclipse darkened the triple audience halls; Chong offered to resign, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 更以沛國之公丘益其封，寵倖愈甚，朝臣咸側目焉。

translations.literal: Moreover the territory of Gongqiu in Pei state was added to his fief; favor and intimacy grew ever greater; court ministers all looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: His fief absorbed Gongqiu in Pei, his influence grew more intoxicating, and fellow ministers watched him with narrowed eyes.

sentences.zh: 河南尹王恂上言：「弘訓太后入廟，合食于景皇帝，齊王攸不得行其子禮。

translations.literal: Governor of Henan Wang Xun submitted a statement: "When Empress Dowager Hongxun enters the temple, she shares sacrifices with Emperor Jing; Prince of Qi You cannot perform rites as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun of Henan argued that once Empress Dowager Hongxun entered the ancestral shrine to share offerings with Emperor Jing, Prince Sima You could no longer mourn her as a son."

sentences.zh: 」充議以為：「禮，諸侯不得祖天子，公子不得禰先君，皆謂奉統承祀，非謂不得復其父祖也。

translations.literal: " Chong deliberated and considered: "By ritual, feudal lords may not take the Son of Heaven as ancestor; sons of the ruling house may not enshrine former rulers as fathers—all this speaks of inheriting the line and receiving sacrifices; it does not mean one may not again regard one's father and grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong countered that ritual barred heirs who inherited the imperial sacrifice from treating earlier rulers as direct fathers—not that a prince could never honor his blood parents."

sentences.zh: 攸身宜服三年喪事，自如臣制。

translations.literal: You personally ought to observe three years' mourning affairs, naturally according to minister regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Sima You should still observe three years' mourning while otherwise behaving as a subject.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏：「若如充議，服子服，行臣制，未有前比。

translations.literal: " The relevant offices memorialized: "If like Chong's deliberation, wearing son's garb yet practicing minister regulations, there is no prior precedent.
translations.idiomatic: " Officials replied that Chong's formula—mourning as a son while acting publicly as a minister—had no precedent."

sentences.zh: 宜如恂表，攸喪服從諸侯之例。

translations.literal: It is fitting to follow Xun's memorial; You's mourning garments should follow feudal lords' precedent.
translations.idiomatic: They urged adopting Wang Xun's memorial so You's mourning would follow the rules for regional princes.

sentences.zh: 」帝從充議。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed Chong's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sided with Chong.

sentences.zh: 伐吳之役，詔充為使持節、假黃鉞、大都督，總統六師，給羽葆、鼓吹、緹幢、兵萬人、騎二千，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎，增參軍、騎司馬各十人，帳下司馬二十人，大車、官騎各三十人。

translations.literal: For the campaign against Wu, an edict appointed Chong Bearer of Credentials, lent credentials with yellow axe, Grand Commander-in-Chief, commander-in-chief of the Six Armies; supplied feather-canopy, drum-and-pipe, yellow banners, ten thousand infantry, two thousand cavalry; established left and right senior administrators, marshals, and staff advisers; increased adjutants and cavalry marshals ten each, twenty marshals of the headquarters guard, thirty large carts and thirty official horsemen each.
translations.idiomatic: For the conquest of Wu the emperor named Chong credential-bearing commander-in-chief of all six armies with the yellow battle-axe, feather canopy, martial bands, silk banners, ten thousand foot soldiers and two thousand horse, full headquarters staff, extra adjutants, escort troops, carriages, and mounted guards.

sentences.zh: 充慮大功不捷，表陳「西有昆夷之患，北有幽並之戍，天下勞擾，年穀不登，興軍致討，懼非其時。

translations.literal: Chong feared the great merit would not succeed; he memorialized stating, "Westward there is trouble from Kun barbarians; northward there are garrisons in You and Bing; all under Heaven is wearied and disturbed; yearly harvests do not ripen; raising armies to undertake punishment—I fear it is not the time.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing failure, Chong memorialized that western tribes, northern garrisons, exhausted taxpayers, and poor harvests made this the wrong moment for war."

sentences.zh: 又臣老邁，非所克堪。

translations.literal: Moreover your subject is old and aged, not what can bear it.
translations.idiomatic: He added that he was too old for such a burden.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「君不行，吾便自出。

translations.literal: " An edict stated, "If you do not go, We shall personally go forth.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered, "If you refuse, I will take the field myself."

sentences.zh: 」充不得已，乃受節鉞，將中軍，為諸軍節度，以冠軍將軍楊濟為副，南屯襄陽。

translations.literal: " Chong had no choice; thereupon he received credentials and axe, led the central army, regulated all armies, with Champion General Yang Ji as deputy, camping south at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong had to accept the command, taking the central army as overall coordinator with champion general Yang Ji as deputy and establishing headquarters south at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 吳江陵諸守皆降，充乃徙屯項。

translations.literal: Wu Jiangling's various defenders all surrendered; Chong thereupon moved camp to Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu's garrisons along the Jiangling front capitulated, Chong shifted his base to Xiang.

sentences.zh: 王浚之克武昌也，充遣使表曰：「吳未可悉定，方夏，江淮下濕，疾疫必起，宜召諸軍，以為後圖。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun had conquered Wuchang, Chong dispatched envoys with a memorial stating, "Wu cannot yet be entirely pacified; it is midsummer; the Jiang and Huai are low and damp; sickness and plague are sure to arise; it is fitting to summon the various armies, planning for later.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Jun seized Wuchang, Chong sent a memorial urging withdrawal: Wu was not yet subdued, summer heat and river damp would breed plague, so recall the armies and plan anew."

sentences.zh: 雖腰斬張華，不足以謝天下。

translations.literal: Even cutting Zhang Hua in two at the waist would not suffice to apologize to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Even executing Zhang Hua would not atone to the realm—an allusion to Zhang Hua's plan for the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 」華豫平吳之策，故充以為言。

translations.literal: " Hua had participated in the plan to pacify Wu; therefore Chong spoke with this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Hua had helped draft the Wu strategy, so Chong cited him to shift blame.

sentences.zh: 中書監荀勖奏，宜如充表。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Xun Xu memorialized that it was fitting to follow Chong's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu as supervisor of the Secretariat backed Chong's memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected it.

sentences.zh: 杜預聞充有奏，馳表固爭，言平在旦夕。

translations.literal: Du Yu heard that Chong had submitted a memorial; he rushed a memorial firmly disputing, stating pacification was within morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Yu learned of Chong's withdrawal plea he sent an urgent counter-memorial insisting victory was hours away.

sentences.zh: 使及至轘轅，而孫皓已降。

translations.literal: When the envoy reached Huanyuan, Sun Hao had already surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Chong's messenger reached the Huanyuan pass, Sun Hao had capitulated.

sentences.zh: 吳平，軍罷。

translations.literal: Wu was pacified; armies were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: With Wu conquered the armies stood down.

sentences.zh: 帝遣侍中程咸犒勞，賜充帛八千匹，增邑八千戶；

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Palace Attendant Cheng Xian to reward the troops; Chong was gifted eight thousand bolts of silk; his fief was increased by eight thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Cheng Xian with rewards: eight thousand bolts of silk for Chong and eight thousand extra households for his fief;

sentences.zh: 分封從孫暢新城亭侯，蓋安陽亭侯；

translations.literal: separately enfeoffed grand-nephew Chang as village marquis of Xincheng, Gai as village marquis of Anyang;
translations.idiomatic: his kinsmen Chang and Gai received minor marquisates at Xincheng and Anyang;

sentences.zh: 弟陽裏亭侯混、從孫關內侯眾增戶邑。

translations.literal: younger brother village marquis of Yangli Hun and grand-nephew secondary marquis within the passes Zhong had households and territories increased.
translations.idiomatic: while his brother Hun and grand-nephew Zhong likewise gained households.

sentences.zh: 充本無南伐之謀，固諫不見用。

translations.literal: Chong fundamentally had no plan for southern expedition; he firmly remonstrated but was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had opposed the southern campaign from the start, yet his warnings went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 及師出而吳平，大慚懼，議欲請罪。

translations.literal: When the army went forth and Wu was pacified, he was greatly ashamed and fearful; he deliberated wishing to request punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies triumphed despite him, he was mortified and considered confessing his obstruction.

sentences.zh: 帝聞充當詣闕，豫幸東堂以待之。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard that Chong was about to attend the palace; beforehand he proceeded to the Eastern Hall to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Chong meant to present himself for punishment, the emperor waited for him in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 罷節鉞、僚佐，仍假鼓吹、麾幢。

translations.literal: Credentials and axe were dismissed, staff assistants; still lent drum-and-pipe and command banners.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped Chong of command credentials and staff but let him keep honorary bands and banners.

sentences.zh: 充與群臣上告成之禮，請有司具其事。

translations.literal: Chong together with the host of ministers submitted the rite of announcing completion, requesting the relevant offices prepare the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Chong joined other ministers in proposing the victory ceremony and asked the bureaus to arrange it.

sentences.zh: 帝謙讓不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor modestly declined and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor modestly refused.

sentences.zh: 充婦廣城君郭槐，性妒忌。

translations.literal: Chong's wife Lady of Guangcheng Guo Huai was by nature jealous.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's wife, Lady Guo Huai of Guangcheng, was fiercely jealous.

sentences.zh: 初，黎民年三歲，乳母抱之當閣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Limin was three years old, the wet nurse held him facing the chamber doorway.
translations.idiomatic: When their son Limin was three, his nurse held him near the chamber entrance.

sentences.zh: 黎民見充入，喜笑，充就而拊之。

translations.literal: Limin saw Chong enter, laughed with joy; Chong approached and patted him.
translations.idiomatic: The boy brightened when Chong entered; Chong stepped over to pat him.

sentences.zh: 槐望見，謂充私乳母，即鞭殺之。

translations.literal: Huai looked and saw, considered that Chong was intimate with the wet nurse, immediately had her whipped to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo assumed Chong was sleeping with the nurse and had her flogged to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 黎民戀念，發病而死。

translations.literal: Limin's longing and attachment mounted; he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: The grieving child sickened and died.

sentences.zh: 後又生男，過期，復為乳母所抱，充以手摩其頭。

translations.literal: Later another boy was born; after the full month, again held by a wet nurse, Chong used his hand to stroke his head.
translations.idiomatic: Another son arrived; after his first month another nurse held him while Chong stroked the infant's head.

sentences.zh: 郭疑乳母，又殺之，兒亦思慕而死。

translations.literal: Guo suspected the wet nurse; again killed her; the child likewise died longing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo suspected that nurse too and killed her; the baby died of grief like the first.

sentences.zh: 充遂無胤嗣。

translations.literal: Chong thereupon had no heir offspring.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Chong was left without male heirs.

sentences.zh: 及薨，槐輒以外孫韓謐為黎民子，奉充後。

translations.literal: When he died, Huai then took grandson-by-daughter Han Mi as Limin's son, to serve Chong's posterity.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong died, Lady Guo installed her grandson Han Mi as heir in Limin's place.

sentences.zh: 郎中令韓咸、中尉曹軫諫槐曰：「禮，大宗無後，以小宗支子後之，無異姓為後之文。

translations.literal: Chief of Gentlemen Han Xian and Commandant of Palace Guards Cao Zhen remonstrated with Huai, saying, "By ritual, when the great lineage lacks heirs, a younger-house collateral son succeeds it; there is no text for taking an heir of different surname.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian and Cao Zhen urged Lady Guo to observe ritual: when the main line lacked heirs a cousin carried it on—law never sanctioned adopting outsiders."

sentences.zh: 無令先公懷腆后土，良史書過，豈不痛心。

translations.literal: Do not let the former Duke harbor shame toward soil and earth; good historians record faults—would it not pain the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Do not make your late husband blush before Heaven and earth while historians record the scandal—that should break your heart."

sentences.zh: 」槐不從。

translations.literal: " Huai did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " She refused.

sentences.zh: 咸等上書求改立嗣，事寢不報。

translations.literal: Xian and others submitted memorials requesting changing the established heir; the affair slept without reply.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized to overturn the adoption, but the petition vanished without answer.

sentences.zh: 槐遂表陳是充遺意。

translations.literal: Huai thereupon memorialized stating this was Chong's dying intention.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo then claimed the adoption had been Chong's dying wish.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔曰：「太宰、魯公充，崇德立勳，勤勞佐命，背世殂隕，每用悼心。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon issued an edict stating, "Grand Tutor, Duke of Lu Chong, elevated virtue and established merit, toiled in assisting the mandate; departed from the age and fell—each time Our mourning heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded: "Grand tutor and duke of Lu Jia Chong served the dynasty with merit until death—Our grief is constant."

sentences.zh: 又胤子早終，世嗣未立。

translations.literal: Moreover heir sons ended early; lineage succession was not established.
translations.idiomatic: His natural heirs died young; the main line stood empty.

sentences.zh: 古者列國無嗣，取始封支庶，以紹其統，而近代更除其國。

translations.literal: In antiquity when feudal states lacked heirs, they took collateral sons from the first enfeoffment to continue its line; yet in recent generations states were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient states without heirs adopted cadets from the founding line, though modern precedent sometimes abolished fiefs outright.

sentences.zh: 至於周之公旦，漢之蕭何，或豫建元子，或封爵元妃，蓋尊顯勳庸，不同常例。

translations.literal: As for Zhou's Duke Dan, Han's Xiao He—some beforehand established eldest sons, some enfeoffed chief consorts—covering honoring and displaying merit achievement, different from ordinary precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's Duke of Zhou and Han's Xiao He enjoyed special privileges—early designation of heirs or honors for wives—because extraordinary merit broke ordinary rules.

sentences.zh: 太宰素取外孫韓謐為世子黎民後。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor long ago took grandson-by-daughter Han Mi as heir-apparent Limin's successor.
translations.idiomatic: The grand tutor had already chosen grandson Han Mi to continue Limin's line.

sentences.zh: 吾退而斷之，外孫骨肉至近，推恩計情，合于人心。

translations.literal: We withdrew and judged it: grandson-by-daughter flesh and bone extremely close; extending grace calculating sentiment accords with men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: We weighed the matter: a daughter's son is close kin, and extending favor to him fits human feeling.

sentences.zh: 其以謐為魯公世孫，以嗣其國。

translations.literal: Let Mi be Duke of Lu's lineage grandson, to succeed its state.
translations.idiomatic: Let Han Mi inherit the duchy of Lu as Chong's designated grandson.

sentences.zh: 自非功如太宰，始封無後如太宰，所取必以己自出不如太宰，皆不得以為比。

translations.literal: Unless merit be like the Grand Tutor, first enfeoffment lacking heirs like the Grand Tutor, those taken must issue from oneself not inferior to the Grand Tutor—none may take this as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Unless merit equals the grand tutor's, unless the founding line fails as his did, and unless the heir springs from one's own issue as Han Mi did, no one may cite this case.

sentences.zh: 」及下禮官議充諡，博士秦秀議諡曰荒，帝不納。

translations.literal: " When it came to handing down to ritual officials deliberating Chong's posthumous title, Erudite Qin Xiu deliberated posthumous title as wasteful; the Emperor did not adopt.
translations.idiomatic: " When ritual officers debated Chong's posthumous name, Erudite Qin Xiu proposed "Desolate"; the emperor rejected it.

sentences.zh: 博士段暢希旨，建議諡曰武，帝乃從之。

translations.literal: Erudite Duan Chang hoped for imperial intention, proposed deliberating posthumous title as martial; the Emperor thereupon followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Duan Chang, angling for imperial favor, suggested "Martial," which the emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 自充薨至葬，賻賜二千萬。

translations.literal: From Chong's death until burial, burial gifts totaled twenty million.
translations.idiomatic: Between his death and burial the court lavished twenty million cash in funeral grants.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，賈后擅權，加充廟備六佾之樂，母郭為宜城君。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui assumed the throne, Empress Jia monopolized authority; Chong's temple was augmented with six-row music; mother Guo became Lady of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui, Empress Jia dominated politics: Chong's shrine gained six rows of ritual dancers and Lady Guo received the title lady of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 及郭氏亡，諡曰宣，特加殊禮。

translations.literal: When the Guo clan lady died, her posthumous title was Declarer; exceptionally added special rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Guo died she received the posthumous name "Declarative" and honors beyond the usual.

sentences.zh: 時人譏之，而莫敢言者。

translations.literal: People of the time mocked this, yet none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries sneered but kept silent.

sentences.zh: 初，充前妻李氏淑美有才行，生二女褒、裕，褒一名荃，裕一名浚。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chong's former wife Lady Li was virtuous and beautiful, possessing talent and conduct; she bore two daughters Bao and Yu; Bao had another name Quan; Yu had another name Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's first wife, Lady Li, was talented and lovely; she bore two daughters—Bao, also called Quan, and Yu, also called Jun.

sentences.zh: 父豐誅，李氏坐流徙。

translations.literal: Her father Feng was executed; Lady Li sat guilty and was banished.
translations.idiomatic: When her father Li Feng was executed, Lady Li was banished as his kin.

sentences.zh: 後娶城陽太守郭配女，即廣城君也。

translations.literal: Later he married the daughter of Administrator of Chengyang Guo Pei—this was Lady of Guangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then married Guo Pei's daughter—Lady Guo Huai of Guangcheng.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，李以大赦得還，帝特詔充置左右夫人，充母亦敕充迎李氏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Li through great amnesty was able to return; the Emperor specially edicted Chong to establish left and right chief wives; Chong's mother also ordered Chong to welcome Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yan took the throne a general amnesty allowed Lady Li home; the emperor ordered Chong to install both women as formal wives, and Chong's mother urged him to bring Li back.

sentences.zh: 郭槐怒，攘袂數充曰：「刊定律令，為佐命之功，我有其分。

translations.literal: Guo Huai raged, rolling up sleeves and enumerating Chong, saying, "Carving and fixing statutes and ordinances, achieving merit as assistant to the mandate—I have my share.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo flared with rage, sleeves rolled up: "I helped codify the laws that founded this dynasty—I earned my place."

sentences.zh: 李那得與我並！

translations.literal: How can Li stand alongside me!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li cannot rank beside me!"

sentences.zh: 」充乃答詔，托以謙沖，不敢當兩夫人盛禮，實畏槐也。

translations.literal: " Chong thereupon replied to the edict, pleading modest yielding, not daring to undertake the grand rite of two chief wives—truly he feared Huai.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong declined the dual-wife arrangement, citing humility when he was simply terrified of Lady Guo.

sentences.zh: 而荃為齊王攸妃，欲令充遣郭而還其母。

translations.literal: Moreover Quan was consort to Prince of Qi You; she wished to make Chong dismiss Guo and return her mother.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter Quan, Prince Sima You's consort, wanted Chong to divorce Lady Guo and restore Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 時沛國劉含母，及帝舅羽林監王虔前妻，皆毌丘儉孫女。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Han's mother in Pei state and the Former Wife of the Emperor's maternal uncle Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Wang Qian were both granddaughters of Guanqiu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Han's mother in Pei and Wang Qian's first wife—both granddaughters of Guanqiu Jian—faced similar disputes.

sentences.zh: 此例既多，質之禮官，俱不能決。

translations.literal: This precedent being numerous, consulting ritual officials, none could decide.
translations.idiomatic: So many cases arose that ritual specialists could not settle them.

sentences.zh: 雖不遣後妻，多異居私通。

translations.literal: Although not dismissing later wives, many dwelt separately and carried on illicit relations.
translations.idiomatic: Men kept later wives in separate households and conducted affairs in secret.

sentences.zh: 充自以宰相為海內準則，乃為李築室於永年裏而不往來。

translations.literal: Chong himself considered the Chancellor as the standard for within the seas; thereupon he built a chamber for Li in Yongnian ward yet did not interact.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, posing as the moral model for the empire, built Lady Li a house in Yongnian ward but never visited.

sentences.zh: 荃、浚每號泣請充，充竟不往。

translations.literal: Quan and Jun each wailed and wept begging Chong; Chong ultimately did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and Jun wept and pleaded; Chong still refused to go.

sentences.zh: 會充當鎮關右，公卿供帳祖道，荃、浚懼充遂去，乃排幔出於坐中，叩頭流血，向充及群僚陳母應還之意。

translations.literal: When Chong was about to garrison the right of the passes, dukes and ministers supplied tents for the farewell road; Quan and Jun feared Chong would then depart; thereupon they pushed aside curtains and emerged within the seating, knocking heads until bleeding, stating to Chong and the host of officials the meaning that mother ought to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong left to command the west, officials lined the road to see him off; fearing he would never return, Quan and Jun burst through the curtains, kowtowing until they bled, begging him before the whole assembly to restore their mother.

sentences.zh: 眾以荃王妃，皆驚起而散。

translations.literal: The multitude because Quan was royal consort, all startled rose and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers, recognizing the prince's consort, fled in confusion.

sentences.zh: 充甚愧愕，遣黃門將宮人扶去。

translations.literal: Chong was greatly ashamed and startled; he dispatched Yellow Gates generals and palace women to support them away.
translations.idiomatic: Mortified, Chong had eunuchs and maids lead the women away.

sentences.zh: 既而郭槐女為皇太子妃，帝乃下詔斷如李比皆不得還，後荃恚憤而薨。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Guo Huai's daughter became the Crown Prince's consort; the Emperor thereupon issued an edict deciding that cases like Li's all might not return; later Quan died of resentment and anger.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lady Guo's daughter became crown princess, the emperor ruled that no banished first wife might return as Lady Li had hoped; Quan died of bitterness soon after.

sentences.zh: 初，槐欲省李氏，充曰：「彼有才氣，卿往不如不往。

translations.literal: Earlier, Huai wished to inspect Lady Li; Chong said, "She possesses talent and spirit; if you go it is not as good as not going.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Guo meant to confront Lady Li, Chong warned, "She outclasses you—stay away or regret it."

sentences.zh: 」及女為妃，槐乃盛威儀而去。

translations.literal: " When the daughter became consort, Huai thereupon in full majestic bearing departed.
translations.idiomatic: " After her daughter became consort, Lady Guo marched over in full state.

sentences.zh: 既入戶，李氏出迎，槐不覺腳屈，因遂再拜。

translations.literal: Having entered the door, Lady Li came out to welcome; Huai unconsciously bent her knees; thereupon performed twice bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, Lady Li greeted her with such grace that Lady Guo's knees buckled and she curtsied twice unthinkingly.

sentences.zh: 自是充每出行，槐輒使人尋之，恐其過李也。

translations.literal: From this whenever Chong went out, Huai always sent people to track him, fearing he would visit Li.
translations.idiomatic: After that Lady Guo had spies follow Chong whenever he left home lest he visit Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 初，充母柳見古今重節義，竟不知充與成濟事，以濟不忠，數追罵之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chong's mother Liu saw that antiquity and present esteem integrity and righteousness; she utterly did not know of Chong's affair with Cheng Ji; considering Ji disloyal, repeatedly chased and reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's mother Lady Liu prized loyalty above all yet never knew her son had ordered Cheng Ji to kill the emperor; she cursed Cheng Ji as a traitor again and again.

sentences.zh: 侍者聞之，無不竊笑。

translations.literal: Attendants hearing it, none did not secretly laugh.
translations.idiomatic: Servants who heard her snickered behind their sleeves.

sentences.zh: 及將亡，充問所欲言，柳曰：「我教汝迎李新婦尚不肯，安問他事！

translations.literal: When about to die, Chong asked what she wished to say; Liu said, "I taught you to welcome the new wife Li and still you would not—why ask other matters!
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed Chong asked her wishes; she snapped, "You would not even fetch Lady Li when I told you—do not speak to me of anything else!"

sentences.zh: 」遂無言。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " She fell silent.

sentences.zh: 及充薨後，李氏二女乃欲令其母祔葬，賈后弗之許也。

translations.literal: When after Chong died, Li's two daughters then wished to make their mother accompany burial; Empress Jia did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: After Chong died the daughters asked to bury Lady Li beside him; Empress Jia refused.

sentences.zh: 及後廢，李氏乃得合葬。

translations.literal: When later she was deposed, Lady Li then was able to share burial.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Empress Jia's fall could Lady Li be interred beside Chong.

sentences.zh: 李氏作《女訓》行於世。

translations.literal: Lady Li composed "Instructions for Women," circulating in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li's "Instructions for Women" circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 謐字長深。

translations.literal: Mi's courtesy name was Changshen.
translations.idiomatic: Han Mi's courtesy name was Changshen.

sentences.zh: 母賈午，充少女也。

translations.literal: His mother was Jia Wu, Chong's youngest daughter.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Jia Wu, Jia Chong's youngest daughter.

sentences.zh: 父韓壽，字德真，南陽堵陽人，魏司徒暨曾孫。

translations.literal: His father Han Shou, courtesy name Dezhen, was a man of Duyang in Nanyang, great-grandson of Wei Minister of Education Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Han Shou (courtesy name Dezhen), came from Duyang in Nanyang and was the great-grandson of Wei minister Han Ji.

sentences.zh: 美姿貌，善容止，賈充辟為司空掾。

translations.literal: Handsome in bearing and looks, skilled in deportment; Jia Chong recruited him as aide to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for looks and graceful manners, he joined Jia Chong's staff as registrar to the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 充每宴賓僚，其女輒於青钅巢中窺之，見壽而悅焉。

translations.literal: Whenever Chong feasted guests and subordinates, his daughter always peered from within the green inlaid screen; seeing Shou she became fond of him.
translations.idiomatic: During Chong's banquets his daughter would spy from behind a pierced green screen; one glimpse of Han Shou captivated her.

sentences.zh: 問其左右識此人不，有一婢說壽姓字，雲是故主人。

translations.literal: She asked those beside her whether they recognized this person; one maid stated Shou's surname and courtesy name, saying he was a former master of the house.
translations.idiomatic: She asked her attendants who he was; a maid supplied Han Shou's name and said he had once served their household.

sentences.zh: 女大感想，發於寤寐。

translations.literal: The girl's great longing arose, issuing from waking and sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: She burned with longing night and day.

sentences.zh: 婢後往壽家，具說女意，並言其女光麗豔逸，端美絕倫。

translations.literal: The maid later went to Shou's house, fully stating the girl's intentions, and moreover spoke of how his daughter was radiant, lovely, sumptuous and unrestrained, upright and beautiful beyond peer.
translations.idiomatic: The maid visited Han Shou and relayed the girl's passion, praising her mistress as incomparably beautiful.

sentences.zh: 壽聞而心動，便令為通殷勤。

translations.literal: Shou heard and his heart moved; then ordered her to convey earnest attentions.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shou agreed and sent her back with intimate messages.

sentences.zh: 婢以白女，女遂潛修音好，厚相贈結，呼壽夕入。

translations.literal: The maid reported to the girl; the girl thereupon secretly cultivated musical goodwill, generously gifting and bonding, summoning Shou to enter by night.
translations.idiomatic: When the maid reported back, the girl began secret correspondence, sent lavish gifts, and invited Han Shou to visit after dark.

sentences.zh: 壽勁捷過人，逾垣而至，家中莫知，惟充覺其女悅暢異于常日。

translations.literal: Shou was vigorous and agile beyond others; he climbed the wall to arrive; none in the household knew; only Chong perceived his daughter's glad expansiveness differed from ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shou scaled the wall—the household noticed nothing—but Chong saw his daughter glowing unlike before.

sentences.zh: 時西域有貢奇香，一著人則經月不歇，帝甚貴之，惟以賜充及大司馬陳騫。

translations.literal: At that time the Western Regions presented exotic incense; once applied to a person it lasted a month without fading; the Emperor greatly prized it; only with it gifted Chong and Grand Marshal Chen Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had received tribute incense from the west whose fragrance clung to the skin for a month; only Chong and Grand Marshal Chen Qian received any.

sentences.zh: 其女密盜以遺壽，充僚屬與壽燕處，聞其芬馥，稱之於充。

translations.literal: His daughter secretly stole it to give to Shou; Chong's subordinates dwelt at ease feasting with Shou, smelled its fragrance, and praised it to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter stole some for Han Shou; when Chong's aides dined with Shou they caught the scent and mentioned it to Chong.

sentences.zh: 自是充意知女與壽通，而其門閣嚴峻，不知所由得入。

translations.literal: From this Chong understood in mind that his daughter was intimate with Shou, yet his gates and towers were strict and severe; he did not know by what means entry had been gained.
translations.idiomatic: Chong realized the affair but could not see how anyone breached his fortified gates.

sentences.zh: 乃夜中陽驚，托言有盜，因使循牆以觀其變。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the night feigning alarm, citing claim of robbers, thereby ordered following the walls to observe the changes.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned a midnight alarm about thieves and ordered patrols along the walls to watch what happened.

sentences.zh: 左右白曰：「無餘異，惟東北角如狐狸行處。

translations.literal: Those beside him reported, saying, "No other strangeness; only the northeast corner like a place foxes traverse.
translations.idiomatic: Guards reported nothing unusual except scratches near the northeast corner "like a fox's path."

sentences.zh: 」充乃考問女之左右，具以狀對。

translations.literal: " Chong thereupon interrogated those beside his daughter; they fully replied with the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Questioning his daughter's maids, Chong extracted the full story.

sentences.zh: 充秘之，遂以女妻壽。

translations.literal: Chong kept it secret; thereupon gave his daughter to Shou as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Chong hushed the scandal and married his daughter to Han Shou.

sentences.zh: 壽官至散騎常侍、河南尹。

translations.literal: Shou's office reached Regular Cavalier Attendant and Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shou rose to regular cavalier attendant and governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 元康初卒，贈驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: He died early in Yuankang; posthumously gifted Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in Yuankang with posthumous appointment as grand general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 謐好學，有才思。

translations.literal: Mi loved learning and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Han Mi was bookish and clever.

sentences.zh: 既為充嗣，繼佐命之後，又賈后專恣，謐權過人主，至乃鎖系黃門侍郎，其為威福如此。

translations.literal: Having become Chong's heir, succeeding after assisting the mandate, moreover Empress Jia monopolized indulgence; Mi's authority surpassed the ruler—to the point of shackling Gentleman Attendants at the Yellow Gates; his wielding favor and terror was thus.
translations.idiomatic: As Chong's heir and with Empress Jia ruling unchecked, Mi wielded more power than the emperor—once shackling a gentleman at the Yellow Gates—such was his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 負其驕寵，奢侈逾度，室宇崇僭，器服珍麗，歌僮舞女，選極一時。

translations.literal: Relying on his arrogant favor, extravagance exceeded measure; chambers and halls lofty and transgressive; vessels and garments precious and lovely; singing boys and dancing girls—selections extreme for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk on privilege he built mansions beyond his rank, stocked treasures, and assembled the finest singers and dancers of the day.

sentences.zh: 開閣延賓。

translations.literal: Opened pavilions and extended guests.
translations.idiomatic: He threw open his salons to host guests.

sentences.zh: 海內輻湊，貴游豪戚及浮競之徙，莫不盡禮事之。

translations.literal: Within the seas spokes converged; noble wanderers, powerful kin, and those who floated in ambition—none failed to exhaust ritual in serving him.
translations.idiomatic: Elite adventurers, powerful in-laws, and opportunists flocked from across the realm to court him.

sentences.zh: 或著文章稱美謐，以方賈誼。

translations.literal: Some composed writings praising Mi, comparing him to Jia Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Some poets compared him to Han dynasty prodigy Jia Yi.

sentences.zh: 渤海石崇歐陽建、滎陽潘岳、吳國陸機陸雲、蘭陵繆征、京兆杜斌摯虞、琅邪諸葛詮、弘農王粹、襄城杜育、南陽鄒捷、齊國左思、清河崔基、沛國劉瑰、汝南和郁周恢、安平牽秀、潁川陳眕、太原郭彰、高陽許猛、彭城劉訥、中山劉輿劉琨皆傅會於謐，號曰二十四友，其餘不得預焉。

translations.literal: Shi Chong and Ouyang Jian of Bohai, Pan Yue of Xingyang, Lu Ji and Lu Yun of Wu, Miao Zheng of Lanling, Du Bin and Zhi Yu of Jingzhao, Zhuge Quan of Langye, Wang Cui of Hongnong, Du Yu of Xiangcheng, Zou Jie of Nanyang, Zuo Si of Qi, Cui Ji of Qinghe, Liu Gui of Pei, He Yu and Zhou Hui of Runan, Qian Xiu of Anping, Chen Zhen of Yingchuan, Guo Zhang of Taiyuan, Xu Meng of Gaoyang, Liu Ne of Pengcheng, and Liu Yu and Liu Kun of Zhongshan all attached to Mi, styled the Twenty-Four Friends; the rest could not join.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong, Ouyang Jian, Pan Yue, the Lu brothers, Zuo Si, Guo Zhang, and other glittering literati from the capital and the provinces all curried favor with Han Mi in a clique known as the Twenty-Four Friends; lesser talents were shut out.

sentences.zh: 尋轉侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 領秘書監如故。

translations.literal: Acting as Supervisor of the Palace Library as before.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his concurrent post as director of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 謐時從帝幸宣武觀校獵，諷尚書于會中召謐受拜，誡左右勿使人知，於是眾疑其有異志矣。

translations.literal: At the time Mi was following the Emperor in visiting Xuanwu Watch for a review hunt; he insinuated to the Masters of Writing to summon Mi in the assembly to receive appointment, admonishing those beside not to let people know; thereupon the multitude suspected he had different intentions.
translations.idiomatic: While Mi accompanied the emperor on a hunt at Xuanwu Watch, his allies quietly arranged through the Masters of Writing to invest him with office mid-event—sworn to secrecy—so courtiers began whispering that Mi harbored treasonous ambitions.

sentences.zh: 謐既親貴，數入二宮，共湣懷太子游處，無屈降心。

translations.literal: Mi having become intimate and noble, repeatedly entered the Two Palaces, together roaming with Crown Prince Minhuai, without submissive yielding heart.
translations.idiomatic: Once favored by both palace complexes, Mi haunted Crown Prince Yu's apartments yet refused to humble himself.

sentences.zh: 常與太子弈棋爭道，成都王穎在坐，正色曰：「皇太子國之儲君，賈謐何得無禮！

translations.literal: He constantly disputed moves playing weiqi with the heir apparent; Prince of Chengdu Ying was seated and said with stern demeanor, "The imperial heir is the state's heir-apparent—how dare Jia Mi be disrespectful!
translations.idiomatic: During one contentious weiqi match Prince Sima Ying of Chengdu rebuked him: "Heir apparent is the foundation of the state—how dare you slight him?"

sentences.zh: 」謐懼，言之於後，遂出穎為平北將軍，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: " Mi feared; spoke of it to the Empress; thereupon Ying was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North, garrisoning Ye.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi complained to Empress Jia, who banished Sima Ying to Ye as general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 及為常侍，侍講東宮，太子意有不悅，謐患之。

translations.literal: When he became Regular Attendant, attending lectures at the Eastern Palace, the heir apparent's intentions showed displeasure; Mi worried over it.
translations.idiomatic: As regular attendant lecturing in the eastern palace, Mi grew anxious at the crown prince's evident dislike.

sentences.zh: 而其家數有妖異，飄風吹其朝服飛上數百丈，墜於中丞台，又蛇出其被中，夜暴雷震其室，柱陷入地，壓毀床帳，謐益恐。

translations.literal: Moreover his household repeatedly had uncanny anomalies; a whirlwind blew his court robes flying upward several hundred zhang, falling on the Censor-in-Chief's terrace; again a snake emerged from within his quilt; at night violent thunder shook his chamber; a pillar sank into earth, crushing and destroying bed curtains; Mi grew ever more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Ill omens multiplied—a gale lofted his court robes onto the censorate tower, a snake crawled from his bedding, lightning shattered his hall—and Mi panicked.

sentences.zh: 及遷侍中，專掌禁內，遂與後成謀，誣陷太子。

translations.literal: When promoted to Palace Attendant, exclusively managing within the forbidden precincts, thereupon with the Empress completed plotting, slandering and trapping the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to palace attendant with access to the inner quarters, he plotted with Empress Jia to frame the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫廢後，以詔召謐於殿前，將戮之。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun deposed the Empress, by edict summoned Mi before the palace hall, about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Sima Lun deposed the empress he summoned Mi to the palace steps for execution.

sentences.zh: 走入西鐘下，呼曰：「阿後救我！

translations.literal: Running beneath the western bell, he cried, "Ah Empress, save me!
translations.idiomatic: He darted beneath the western bell tower screaming, "Mother empress, save me!"

sentences.zh: 」乃就斬之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they proceeded to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: " They dragged him out and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 韓壽少弟蔚有器望，及壽兄鞏令保、弟散騎侍郎預、吳王友鑒、謐母賈午皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Han Shou's youngest younger brother Wei had vessel and reputation; as well as Shou's elder brother Magistrate of Gong county Bao, younger brother Regular Cavalier Attendant Yu, Friend to the Prince of Wu Jian, Mi's mother Jia Wu—all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wei, Han Bao, Han Yu, Jian who served as friend to the prince of Wu, and Mi's mother Jia Wu were all executed alongside the clan.

sentences.zh: 初，充伐吳時，嘗屯項城，軍中忽失充所在。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chong campaigned against Wu, he once garrisoned Xiang city; within the army suddenly Chong's whereabouts were lost.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wu campaign Chong once headquartered at Xiang—one day he vanished from camp.

sentences.zh: 充帳下都督周勤時晝寢，夢見百餘人錄充，引入一逕。

translations.literal: Chong's headquarters commander Zhou Qin at that time napped by day and dreamed of over a hundred persons seizing Chong, leading him into a path.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Zhou Qin napped and dreamed of a hundred bailiffs hauling Chong down a narrow lane.

sentences.zh: 勤驚覺，聞失充，乃出尋索，忽睹所夢之道。

translations.literal: Qin startled awake, heard that Chong was lost; thereupon went out to search; suddenly beheld the path of his dream.
translations.idiomatic: Startled awake to news that Chong was missing, Zhou Qin rushed out and recognized the dream path.

sentences.zh: 遂往求之。

translations.literal: Thereupon went to seek him.
translations.idiomatic: He followed it.

sentences.zh: 果見充行至一府舍，侍衛甚盛。

translations.literal: Indeed saw Chong walking until reaching a prefectural compound; guards were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He found Chong entering a guarded mansion.

sentences.zh: 府公南南坐，聲色甚曆，謂充曰：「將亂吾家事，必爾與荀勖，既惑吾子，又亂吾孫。

translations.literal: The prefect sat facing south; voice and expression very stern; said to Chong, "About to disorder my household affairs—surely you and Xun Xu; having deluded my son, again disordering my grandson.
translations.idiomatic: A stern official faced south and accused Chong: "You and Xun Xu will ruin my house—you misled my heir and now poison my grandson."

sentences.zh: 間使任愷黜汝而不去，又使庾純詈汝而不改。

translations.literal: Secretly caused Ren Kai to demote you yet you did not depart; again caused Yu Chun to revile you yet you did not reform.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kai tried to exile you and Yu Chun cursed you in court—yet you never changed."

sentences.zh: 今吳寇當平，汝方表斬張華。

translations.literal: Now Wu marauders ought to be pacified; you just memorialized beheading Zhang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Even as Wu falls you demand Zhang Hua's head to sabotage victory."

sentences.zh: 汝之暗戇，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Your dark stupidity—all is of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Every scheme of yours is this foolish."

sentences.zh: 若不悛慎，當旦夕加罪。

translations.literal: If you do not reform and be cautious, shortly morning and evening punishment will be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Unless you mend your ways, punishment comes at once."

sentences.zh: 」充因叩頭流血，公曰：「汝所以延日月而名器如此者，是衛府之勳耳。

translations.literal: " Chong therefore knocked head until bleeding; the prefect said, "That by which you prolong days and months yet vessels and titles are thus—is the merit of the Wei mansion alone.
translations.idiomatic: Chong kowtowed until he bled; the specter said, "You owe rank and life only to service rendered under Wei."

sentences.zh: 終當使系嗣死于鐘虡之間，大子斃于金酒之中，小子困於枯木之下。

translations.literal: In the end shall cause heir descendants to die between bell racks; the grand heir to perish within golden wine; the lesser son to be trapped beneath dry wood.
translations.idiomatic: Your heir will die beneath the bell, your crown prince will swallow poisoned wine, your cadets will perish like dry wood."

sentences.zh: 荀勖亦宜同，然其先德小濃。

translations.literal: Xun Xu ought likewise to share the same; yet his ancestors' virtue is slightly thick.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu shares your guilt, though his ancestors earned slightly more grace."

sentences.zh: 故在汝後，數世之外，國嗣亦替。
