translations.literal: Therefore behind you; beyond several generations, state heirs likewise are replaced.
translations.idiomatic: His line falls after yours; within generations his house too ends."

sentences.zh: 」言畢，命去。

translations.literal: " Speech finished, ordered him to depart.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he dismissed Chong.

sentences.zh: 充忽然得還營，顏色憔悴，性理昏喪，經日乃復。

translations.literal: Chong suddenly obtained return to camp; facial color haggard; disposition and sense darkened and lost; after days then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Chong woke back in camp, drained and confused for days.

sentences.zh: 及是，謐死于鐘下，賈后服金酒而死，賈午考竟用大杖。

translations.literal: When it came to this, Mi died beneath the bell; Empress Jia drank golden wine and died; Jia Wu was interrogated to the limit with great clubs.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Mi died beneath that bell, Empress Jia drank poison, and Jia Wu was beaten to death—each doom matching the curse.

sentences.zh: 終皆如所言。

translations.literal: In the end all was as spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Every prophecy came true.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫之敗，朝廷追述充勳，議立其後。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun was defeated, the court traced Chong's merit and deliberated establishing his posterity.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Lun fell the court remembered Chong's service and debated restoring his line.

sentences.zh: 欲以充從孫散騎侍郎眾為嗣，眾陽狂自免。

translations.literal: They wished to take Chong's grand-nephew Regular Cavalier Attendant Zhong as heir; Zhong feigned madness to exempt himself.
translations.idiomatic: Officials proposed Chong's grand-nephew Zhong as heir, but he feigned madness to escape.

sentences.zh: 以子禿後充，封魯公，又病死。

translations.literal: Using son Tu to succeed Chong, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu; again died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tu inherited the duchy of Lu but soon died young.

sentences.zh: 永興中，立充從曾孫湛為魯公，奉充後，遭亂死，國除。

translations.literal: During Yongxing, established Chong's great-grand-nephew Zhan as Duke of Lu, serving Chong's posterity; encountered turmoil and died; state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxing great-grand-nephew Zhan revived the title until war killed him and ended the fief.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，人為充等謠曰：「賈、裴、王，亂紀綱。

translations.literal: In Taishi, people made for Chong and others a rhyme: "Jia, Pei, Wang—disorder statutes and guidelines.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi-era rhymesters sang: "Jia, Pei, Wang—chaos in the law."

sentences.zh: 王、裴、賈，濟天下。

translations.literal: Wang, Pei, Jia—succor all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, Pei, Jia—they rescue the realm."

sentences.zh: 」言亡魏而成晉也。

translations.literal: " Speaking of Wei perishing and Jin completing.
translations.idiomatic: " Meaning Wei fell so Jin might rise.

sentences.zh: 充弟混，字宮奇，篤厚自守，無殊才能。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Hun, courtesy name Gongqi, was honest and thick, guarding himself; lacked unusual talent or ability.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's younger brother Hun (courtesy Gongqi) was steady but undistinguished.

sentences.zh: 太康中，為宗正卿。

translations.literal: During Taikang, he was Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taikang he directed the bureau of imperial clan affairs.

sentences.zh: 曆鎮軍將軍，領城門校尉，加侍中，封永平侯。

translations.literal: He served as General Who Guards the Army, concurrently Colonel of the City Gates, added Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as marquis of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general who guards the army, colonel of the city gates, palace attendant, and marquis of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈中軍大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously gifted Grand General of the Central Army, parity of ceremony to the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received grand general of the central army with Three Offices honors.

sentences.zh: 充從子彝、遵並有鑒裁，俱為黃門郎。

translations.literal: Chong's nephews Yi and Zun both had judgment and discernment; both were Gentlemen at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Nephews Yi and Zun were discerning critics who both served as gentlemen at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 遵弟模最知名。

translations.literal: Zun's younger brother Mo was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, Zun's younger brother, became the famous one.

sentences.zh: 模字思範，少有志尚。

translations.literal: Mo's courtesy name was Sifan; in youth he had ambitions and aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mo (courtesy Sifan) aimed high from youth.

sentences.zh: 頗覽載籍，而沈深有智算，確然難奪。

translations.literal: Quite perused records and texts; yet deep and profound with wisdom and calculation; firm and certain, hard to wrest away.
translations.idiomatic: Well read and quietly calculating, he held firm opinions.

sentences.zh: 深為充所信愛，每事籌之焉。

translations.literal: Deeply trusted and loved by Chong; in each affair planned with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong relied on him for every decision.

sentences.zh: 充年衰疾劇，恆憂己諡傳，模曰：「是非久自見，不可掩也。

translations.literal: Chong's years declined and illness acute; constantly worried about his posthumous title transmission; Mo said, "Right and wrong long self appear; cannot be covered.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong fretted over his posthumous name, Mo answered, "Truth outs with time—it cannot be buried."

sentences.zh: 」起家為邵陵令，遂曆事二宮尚書吏部郎，以公事免，起為車騎司馬。

translations.literal: " Rising from home as Magistrate of Shaoling; thereupon served Two Palaces as Gentleman of Personnel Selection of the Masters of Writing; dismissed because of public affairs; raised again as Marshal of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: " He began as magistrate of Shaoling, served both palaces as personnel director of the Masters of Writing, briefly fell from office, then became marshal to the general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 豫誅楊駿，封平陽鄉侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Participated in executing Yang Jun; enfeoffed as village marquis of Pingyang; fief one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For helping execute Yang Jun he became village marquis of Pingyang with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 及楚王瑋矯詔害汝南王亮、太保衛瓘，詔使模將中騶二百人救之。

translations.literal: When Prince Chu Wei forged an edict harming Prince of Runan Liang and Grand Tutor Wei Guan, an edict ordered Mo to lead two hundred mounted messengers of the central guard to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima Wei forged orders against Sima Liang and Wei Guan, Mo led two hundred imperial escort riders in a rescue attempt.

sentences.zh: 是時賈后既豫朝政，欲委信親黨，拜模散騎常侍，二日擢為侍中。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Jia already participated in court governance; wishing to entrust trust to kin and partisans, appointed Mo Regular Cavalier Attendant; within two days promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia, already meddling in policy, promoted Mo to regular cavalier attendant and within two days to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 模乃盡心匡弼，推張華、裴顗同心輔政。

translations.literal: Mo thereupon exhausted heart in correcting assistance; recommending Zhang Hua and Pei Yi with united hearts to assist governance.
translations.idiomatic: Mo threw his weight behind Zhang Hua and Pei Yi as co-regents.

sentences.zh: 數年之中，朝野寧靜，模之力也。

translations.literal: Within several years, court and wilds were tranquil and quiet—Mo's force.
translations.idiomatic: For several years court and countryside stayed calm thanks largely to Mo.

sentences.zh: 乃加授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Thereupon additionally invested as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He received the additional title grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 然模潛執權勢，外形欲遠之，每有啟奏賈后事，入輒取急，或托疾以避之。

translations.literal: Yet Mo secretly grasped power and influence; outward form wishing to distance from it; whenever there were memorials reporting Empress Jia's affairs, entering then immediately took urgent leave, or feigned illness to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Mo hoarded influence while pretending distance—whenever petitioners raised Empress Jia's misconduct he pleaded sudden illness.

sentences.zh: 至於素有嫌忿，多所中陷，朝廷甚憚之。

translations.literal: As for those who long had resentment and anger, many were struck and trapped; the court greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who crossed him suffered trumped-up charges; the bureaucracy feared him.

sentences.zh: 加貪冒聚斂，富擬王公。

translations.literal: Added greedy risk and accumulated collection; wealth rivaled kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy extortion made him as rich as princes.

sentences.zh: 但賈后性甚強暴，模每盡言為陳禍福，後不能從，反謂模毀己。

translations.literal: But Empress Jia's nature was very violent and cruel; Mo often exhausted speech to explain calamity and blessing; the Empress could not follow; instead said Mo slandered herself.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia was vicious; Mo warned her honestly of consequences until she accused him of slandering her.

sentences.zh: 於是委任之情日衰，而讒間之徒遂進。

translations.literal: Thereupon entrusted duty sentiment daily declined; while slanderous divisive followers then advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Her trust faded while flatterers advanced.

sentences.zh: 模不得志，憂憤成疾。

translations.literal: Mo did not obtain his ambitions; worry and anger became illness.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated and embittered, Mo fell ill.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰成。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously gifted General of Chariots and Cavalry, opener of office with parity to Three Offices; posthumous title Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously named general of chariots and cavalry with independent headquarters and posthumous epithet "Accomplished."

sentences.zh: 子遊字彥將嗣，曆官太子侍講、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Son You, courtesy name Yanjiang, succeeded; served as Lecturer to the Heir Apparent, Supernumerary Regular Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son You (courtesy Yanjiang) inherited his titles and served as lecturer to the heir apparent and supernumerary cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 郭彰，字叔武，太原人，賈后從舅也。

translations.literal: Guo Zhang, courtesy name Shuwu, a man of Taiyuan, was Empress Jia's maternal cousin-by-marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhang (courtesy Shuwu) of Taiyuan was Empress Jia's uncle by marriage.

sentences.zh: 與賈充素相親遇，充妻待彰若同生。

translations.literal: With Jia Chong long mutually intimate and favored; Chong's wife treated Zhang as if same-born.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had long favored him, and Lady Guo treated him like a full brother.

sentences.zh: 曆散騎常侍、尚書、衛將軍，封冠軍縣侯。

translations.literal: He served as Regular Cavalier Attendant, Masters of Writing, General Who Guards the Army; enfeoffed as county marquis of Champion.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through regular cavalier attendant and minister posts to general who guards the army and county marquis of Champion.

sentences.zh: 及賈后專朝，彰豫參權勢，物情歸附，賓客盈門。

translations.literal: When Empress Jia monopolized the court, Zhang participated in power and influence; objects of sentiment attached; guests filled the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Jia's dictatorship he shared her power; clients packed his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 世人稱為「賈郭」，謂謐及彰也。

translations.literal: People of the age called them "Jia-Guo," referring to Mi and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: People paired him with the Jia clan as the "Jia-Guo" faction alongside Han Mi.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He died with posthumous epithet "Fierce."

sentences.zh: 楊駿，字文長，弘農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Jun, courtesy name Wenzhang, was a man of Huayin in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun (courtesy Wenzhang) came from Huayin in Hongnong commandery.

sentences.zh: 少以王官為高陸令，驍騎、鎮軍二府司馬。

translations.literal: In youth by royal official appointment was Magistrate of Gaolu; marshal to the two offices of Agile Cavalry and Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He began as magistrate of Gaolu on princely nomination, then served as marshal to the agile cavalry and army-guarding headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後以後父超居重位，自鎮軍將軍遷車騎將軍，封臨晉侯。

translations.literal: Later because he was empress's father he rose beyond rank; from General Who Guards the Army promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry; enfeoffed as marquis of Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: As empress dowager's father he vaulted to grand general of chariots and cavalry and marquis of Linjin.

sentences.zh: 識者議之曰：「夫封建諸侯，所以籓屏王室也。

translations.literal: Those who understood criticized it, saying, "As for enfeoffing feudal lords—the means thereby is to screen and shield the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said: "Feudal enfeoffments exist to shield the throne."

sentences.zh: 后妃，所以供粢盛，弘內教也。

translations.literal: Empresses and consorts—the means thereby is to supply grain offerings and extend inner teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts supply ancestral offerings and spread virtue within the palace."

sentences.zh: 後父始封而以臨晉為侯，兆於亂矣。

translations.literal: An empress's father receiving first enfeoffment yet taking Linjin as marquis—omen toward chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Giving an empress's father Linjin as his first fief foretells disaster."

sentences.zh: 」尚書褚䂮、郭奕並表駿小器，不可以任社稷之重。

translations.literal: " Ministers of Writing Chu Xie and Guo Yi together memorialized that Jun was small-vessel; could not be entrusted with the altars' heaviness.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Chu Xie and Guo Yi memorialized that Yang Jun lacked stature for the realm's burdens."

sentences.zh: 武帝不從。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu ignored them.

sentences.zh: 帝自太康以後，天下無事，不復留心萬機，惟耽酒色，始寵後黨，請謁公行。

translations.literal: The Emperor from Taikang onward, all under Heaven without affairs, no longer kept heart on myriad mechanisms; only addicted to wine and sex; began favoring empress faction; requests and visits openly practiced.
translations.idiomatic: After Taikang the emperor ignored government, drowned in wine and women, elevated the empress's clan, and sold offices openly.

sentences.zh: 而駿及珧、濟勢傾天下，時人有「三楊」之號。

translations.literal: And Jun together with Yao and Ji's influence overturned all under Heaven; people of the time had the sobriquet "Three Yangs."
translations.idiomatic: Jun and his brothers Yao and Ji dominated the realm—the "Three Yangs."

sentences.zh: 及帝疾篤，未有顧命，佐命功臣，皆已沒矣，朝臣惶惑，計無所從。

translations.literal: When the Emperor grew gravely ill, there was no testamentary charge; merit ministers who assisted the mandate had all already perished; court ministers were fearful and confused; stratagem had nowhere from which to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor sank without naming regents—his veteran advisers gone—officials panicked with no plan.

sentences.zh: 而駿盡斥群公，親侍左右。

translations.literal: Yet Jun dismissed all dukes and personally attended left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun drove senior ministers away and alone attended the dying emperor.

sentences.zh: 因輒改易公卿，樹其心腹。

translations.literal: Thereupon arbitrarily replaced dukes and ministers, planting his inner-heart men.
translations.idiomatic: He reshuffled the high command and packed offices with loyalists.

sentences.zh: 會帝小間，見所用者非，乃正色謂駿曰：「何得便爾！

translations.literal: When it happened the Emperor had slight respite, saw those employed were wrong; then with stern demeanor said to Jun, "How dare it be thus!
translations.idiomatic: During a lucid moment the emperor saw Jun's appointments and snapped, "How dare you!"

sentences.zh: 」乃詔中書，以汝南王亮與駿夾輔王室。

translations.literal: " Thereupon edicted the Masters of Writing that Prince of Runan Liang with Jun flank-assist the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the Secretariat to name Prince Sima Liang of Runan co-regent with Yang Jun."

sentences.zh: 駿恐失權寵，從中書借詔觀之，得便藏匿。

translations.literal: Jun feared losing power and favor; borrowed the edict from the Masters of Writing to view it; obtained convenience and hid it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing loss of power, Jun borrowed the draft edict from the Secretariat and hid it.

sentences.zh: 中書監華廙恐懼，自往索之，終不肯與。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Hua Yi was fearful; personally went to demand it; to the end refused to give.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yi demanded the edict back in person; Jun refused.

sentences.zh: 信宿之間，上疾遂篤，後乃奏帝以駿輔政，帝頷之。

translations.literal: Within two nights, the Superior's illness then became grave; the Empress thereupon memorialized the Emperor to have Jun assist governance; the Emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the emperor worsened; Empress Yang memorialized to make Jun regent and received a nod.

sentences.zh: 便召中書監華暠、令何劭，口宣帝旨使作遺詔，曰：「昔伊望作佐，勳垂不朽；

translations.literal: Then summoned Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Hua Gao and Director He Shao, orally proclaimed imperial intention ordering them to compose testament edict, stating, "Formerly Yi and Wang acted as assistants; merit hangs imperishable;
translations.idiomatic: She summoned Hua Yi and He Shao to draft a will: "Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou served as regents whose fame endures."

sentences.zh: 周霍拜命，名冠往代。

translations.literal: Zhou and Huo received mandate; names capped former ages.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou and Huo regencies crowned their eras."

sentences.zh: 侍中、車騎將軍、行太子太保，領前將軍楊駿，經德履吉，鑒識明遠，毗翼二宮，忠肅茂著，宜正位上臺，擬跡阿衡。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, conducting Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, concurrently General of the Van Yang Jun—threads virtue treads auspiciousness; judgment and insight bright and far-reaching; wings both palaces; loyalty and solemnity luxuriantly manifest—ought to rectify position on upper terrace, trace footsteps of Yi Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant, general of chariots and cavalry, acting junior tutor and van leader Yang Jun served both palaces with loyalty—install him as chief minister like Yi Yin."

sentences.zh: 其以駿為太尉、太子太傅、假節、都督中外諸軍事，侍中、錄尚書、領前將軍如故。

translations.literal: Let Jun be Grand Commandant, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, lent credentials, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without; Palace Attendant, recording Masters of Writing, concurrently General of the Van as before.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint Jun grand commandant, grand tutor to the heir, commander of all armies with imperial baton, retaining his palace attendant, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and van leader posts."

sentences.zh: 置參軍六人、步兵三千人、騎千人，移止前衛將軍珧故府。

translations.literal: Establish six adjutants, three thousand infantry, one thousand cavalry; moved quarters to former mansion of former Van Leader General Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Grant six staff officers, three thousand foot, one thousand horse, and headquarters in former General Yang Yao's compound."

sentences.zh: 若止宿殿中宜有翼衛，其差左右衛三部司馬各二十人、殿中都尉司馬十人給駿，令得持兵仗出入。

translations.literal: If lodging overnight within the hall ought to have wing guards; assign left and right guards three departments' marshals twenty each, hall Central Commandant marshals ten for Jun, ordering him able to bear weapons entering and exiting.
translations.idiomatic: If he sleeps in the palace, assign forty guards from the left and right guards plus ten hall marshals so he may carry arms within the halls."

sentences.zh: 」詔成，後對暠、劭以呈帝，帝親視而無言。

translations.literal: " When edict was completed, the Empress faced Gao and Shao to present to the Emperor; the Emperor personally viewed and spoke nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " When the edict was ready Empress Yang showed it with Hua Yi and He Shao; the emperor looked it over in silence.

sentences.zh: 自是二日而崩，駿遂當寄託之重，居太極殿。

translations.literal: From this within two days he collapsed; Jun thereupon bore entrusted heaviness; dwelled in Supreme Ultimate Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the emperor died; Jun assumed regency and occupied the Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 梓宮將殯，六宮出辭，而駿不下殿，以武賁百人自衛。

translations.literal: When the catalpa coffin was about to be buried, Six Palaces went forth to bid farewell; yet Jun did not descend the hall; with martial awe hundred men self-guarded.
translations.idiomatic: When the catafalque left the palace women came to mourn but Jun never left the hall, ringed by a hundred guardsmen.

sentences.zh: 不恭之跡，自此而始。

translations.literal: Traces of irreverence began from this.
translations.idiomatic: His arrogance began here.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，進駿為太傅、大都督、假黃鉞，錄朝政，百官總己。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui assumed the throne, Jun was advanced to Grand Tutor, Grand Commander-in-Chief, lent yellow axe; recorded court governance; hundred officials answered to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui promoted Jun to grand tutor and commander-in-chief with the yellow axe, controlling government while officials answered only to him.

sentences.zh: 慮左右間己，乃以其甥段廣、張劭為近侍之職。

translations.literal: Fearing those beside him would estrange himself; thereupon made his nephews-by-marriage Duan Guang and Zhang Shao hold intimate attendant duties.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing intrigue he installed nephews Duan Guang and Zhang Shao as palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 凡有詔命，帝省訖，入呈太后，然後乃出。

translations.literal: Whenever there were edicts and commands, the Emperor examined finished; entered presenting Empress Dowager; then afterward issued.
translations.idiomatic: Every edict passed before Emperor Hui, then Empress Dowager Yang, before publication.

sentences.zh: 駿知賈后情性難制，甚畏憚之。

translations.literal: Jun knew Empress Jia's disposition was hard to control; greatly feared and dreaded her.
translations.idiomatic: Jun dreaded Empress Jia's uncontrollable temper.

sentences.zh: 又多樹親黨，皆領禁兵。

translations.literal: Moreover extensively planted kin partisans; all commanded forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: He packed the palace guard with kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 於是公室怨望，天下憤然矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ducal house resented and hoped; all under Heaven indignant.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan seethed and the realm grew furious.

sentences.zh: 駿弟珧、濟並有俊才，數相諫止，駿不能用，因廢於家。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brothers Yao and Ji both had outstanding talent; repeatedly mutually remonstrated and stopped; Jun could not employ; therefore dismissed at home.
translations.idiomatic: His talented brothers Yao and Ji urged restraint until Jun sidelined them.

sentences.zh: 駿暗于古義，動違舊典。

translations.literal: Jun was dark regarding ancient meanings; movements violated old canons.
translations.idiomatic: Jun ignored precedent at every turn.

sentences.zh: 武帝崩未逾年而改元，議者咸以為違《春秋》逾年書即位之義。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu collapsed not yet exceeding a year yet changed era name; deliberators all considered it violated Spring and Autumn Annals' meaning of recording enthronement after exceeding year.
translations.idiomatic: Changing the era name before completing mourning violated the Spring and Autumn rule.

sentences.zh: 朝廷惜於前失，令史官沒之，故明年正月復改年焉。

translations.literal: The court regretted the prior fault; ordered historians to suppress it; therefore next year's first month again changed year.
translations.idiomatic: The court hushed the historians and issued another era change the next New Year.

sentences.zh: 殿中中郎孟觀、李肇，素不為駿所禮，陰構駿將圖社稷。

translations.literal: Palace Gentlemen Meng Guan and Li Zhao, long not treated with ritual by Jun, secretly framed Jun about to plot the altars.
translations.idiomatic: Palace gentlemen Meng Guan and Li Zhao—men Jun had snubbed—claimed he plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 賈后欲預政事，而憚駿未得逞其所欲，又不肯以婦道事皇太后。

translations.literal: Empress Jia wished to participate in administrative affairs; yet dreaded Jun not yet achieving her desires; also unwilling to serve Empress Dowager by wives' way.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia wanted power but Yang Jun blocked her and refused to defer to Empress Dowager Yang.

sentences.zh: 黃門董猛，始自帝之為太子即為寺人監，在東宮給事于賈后。

translations.literal: Yellow Gates Dong Meng, from when the Emperor was heir apparent was already Eunuch Supervisor; in Eastern Palace served Empress Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Dong Meng had served Empress Jia since crown prince days.

sentences.zh: 後密通消息於猛，謀廢太后。

translations.literal: The Empress secretly communicated messages to Meng; plotted deposing Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: She used Meng to plot the empress dowager's ouster.

sentences.zh: 猛乃與肇、觀潛相結托。

translations.literal: Meng thereupon with Zhao and Guan secretly mutually bonded and entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Meng allied secretly with Li Zhao and Meng Guan.

sentences.zh: 賈后又令肇報大司馬、汝南王亮，使連兵討駿。

translations.literal: Empress Jia again ordered Zhao to report to Grand Marshal, Prince of Runan Liang, ordering linked armies to punish Jun.
translations.idiomatic: She told Li Zhao to summon Grand Marshal Sima Liang against Jun.

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「駿之凶暴，死亡無日，不足憂也。

translations.literal: Liang said, "Jun's fierce cruelty—death has no day—not worth worrying.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Liang replied, "Jun's brutality will doom him soon—ignore him."

sentences.zh: 」肇報楚王瑋，瑋然之。

translations.literal: " Zhao reported to Prince Chu Wei; Wei approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Zhao won Prince Sima Wei of Chu's support.

sentences.zh: 於是求入朝，駿素憚瑋，先欲召入，防其為變，因遂聽之。

translations.literal: Thereupon requested entering court; Jun long dreaded Wei; first wished to summon him in; guard against him causing change; therefore then permitted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei requested audience Jun—who feared him—allowed entry to prevent defiance.

sentences.zh: 及瑋至，觀、肇乃啟帝，夜作詔，中外戒嚴，遣使奉詔廢駿，以侯就第。

translations.literal: When Wei arrived, Guan and Zhao then opened to the Emperor; night composed edict; within and without martial law; dispatched envoys bearing edict deposing Jun; as marquis proceed to mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei arrived Guan and Zhao secured Emperor Hui's warrant by night, mobilized the guards, and ordered Jun stripped to his marquisate.

sentences.zh: 東安公繇率殿中四百人隨其後以討駿。

translations.literal: Duke of Dong'an You led four hundred palace attendants following behind to punish Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Sima You of Dong'an followed with four hundred palace troops.

sentences.zh: 段廣跪而言於帝曰：「楊駿受恩先帝，竭心輔政。

translations.literal: Duan Guang knelt and spoke to the Emperor, saying, "Yang Jun received grace from former emperor; exhausted heart assisting governance.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Guang knelt before Emperor Hui: "Yang Jun served your father faithfully."

sentences.zh: 且孤公無子，豈有反理？

translations.literal: Moreover orphaned lord without sons—how could there be rebellion principle?
translations.idiomatic: A childless widower hardly rebels."

sentences.zh: 願陛下審之。

translations.literal: Wish Your Majesty examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Consider carefully, sire."

sentences.zh: 」帝不答。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Hui said nothing.

sentences.zh: 時駿居曹爽故府，在武庫南，聞內有變，召眾官議之。

translations.literal: At that time Jun dwelt in Cao Shuang's former mansion, south of the armory; hearing change within, summoned host of officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was quartered in Cao Shuang's old compound near the armory when news of the coup arrived.

sentences.zh: 太傅主簿硃振說駿曰：「今內有變，其趣可知，必是閹豎為賈后設謀，不利於公。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor chief clerk Zhu Zhen persuaded Jun, saying, "Now within there is change; its tendency can be known—it must be eunuchs plotting for Empress Jia, not benefiting lord.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Zhu Zhen urged Jun: "Palace eunuchs serve Empress Jia—move against them now."

sentences.zh: 宜燒雲龍門以示威，索造事都首，開萬春門，引東宮及外營兵，公自擁翼皇太子，入宮取奸人。

translations.literal: It is fitting to burn Cloud Dragon Gate to display might; seek chief instigators; open Wanchun Gate; lead Eastern Palace and outer camp troops; lord personally embrace and wing Crown Prince; enter palace seize wicked men.
translations.idiomatic: Burn Cloud Dragon Gate as signal, open Wanchun Gate, march eastern-palace troops beside the heir apparent, and arrest the plotters."

sentences.zh: 殿內震懼，必斬送之，可以免難。

translations.literal: Within the hall they will tremble in fear; surely behead and deliver them; can thereby escape calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Panic inside would force them to surrender heads—your only escape."

sentences.zh: 」駿素怯懦，不決，乃曰：「魏明帝造此大功，奈何燒之！

translations.literal: " Jun long cowardly and weak, undecided; then said, "Wei Mingdi built this great achievement—how burn it!
translations.idiomatic: " Jun quailed: "Mingdi built that gate—I cannot burn it!"

sentences.zh: 」侍中傅祗夜白駿，請與武茂俱入雲龍門觀察事勢。

translations.literal: " Palace Attendant Fu Zhi night reported to Jun, requesting together with Wu Mao both enter Cloud Dragon Gate observe affair situation.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Zhi offered to enter Cloud Dragon Gate with Wu Mao to scout.

sentences.zh: 祗因謂群僚「宮中不宜空」，便起揖，於是皆走。

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon told host of colleagues "within palace ought not be empty"; then rose bowing; thereupon all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi told colleagues the palace could not be abandoned—then bowed and fled; others scattered.

sentences.zh: 尋而殿中兵出，燒駿府，又令弩士於閣上臨駿府而射之，駿兵皆不得出。

translations.literal: Soon palace troops emerged, burned Jun's mansion; again ordered crossbowmen on towers overlooking Jun's mansion to shoot them; Jun's troops all could not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Palace troops torched his compound and shot anyone trying to flee.

sentences.zh: 駿逃於馬廄，以戟殺之。

translations.literal: Jun fled to horse stable; with halberd killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They cornered Jun in the stables and speared him.

sentences.zh: 觀等受賈后密旨，誅駿親黨，皆夷三族，死者數千人。

translations.literal: Guan and others received Empress Jia's secret instructions; executed Jun's intimate partisans; all exterminated three clans; dead numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on Empress Jia's orders Guan annihilated Jun's faction—thousands died across three kin circles.

sentences.zh: 又令李肇焚駿家私書，賈后不欲令武帝顧命手詔聞于四海也。

translations.literal: Again ordered Li Zhao burn Jun family's private writings; Empress Jia did not wish to let Emperor Wu's testamentary handwritten edict be heard within four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao burned Jun's papers to hide Emperor Wu's deathbed instructions.

sentences.zh: 駿既誅，莫敢收者，惟太傅舍人巴西閻纂殯斂之。

translations.literal: Jun having been executed, none dared collect him; only Grand Tutor retainer Yan Zuan of Baxi buried and encoffined him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yan Zuan dared bury Yang Jun.

sentences.zh: 初，駿征高士孫登，遺以布被。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jun summoned lofty gentleman Sun Deng; gifted him cloth quilt.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Jun had summoned recluse Sun Deng and gifted a quilt.

sentences.zh: 登截被於門，大呼曰：「斫斫刺刺！

translations.literal: Deng cut the quilt at the gate, greatly shouting, saying, "Chop chop stab stab!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng shredded it at the gate shouting "Blades and spearheads!"

sentences.zh: 」旬日托疾詐死，及是，其言果驗。

translations.literal: " Within ten days feigned illness fake death; when it came to this, his words indeed verified.
translations.idiomatic: " Ten days later he feigned death—prophecy fulfilled when halberds slew Jun.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，溫縣有人如狂，造書曰：「光光文長，大戟為牆。

translations.literal: During Yongxi, a man in Wen county like madness composed writing saying, "Bright bright Wenzhang; great halberds as walls.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi a Wen county madman circulated a rhyme: "Glittering Wenzhang—halberds for walls."

sentences.zh: 毒藥雖行，戟還自傷。

translations.literal: Poison drugs although proceed; halberds return self-harming.
translations.idiomatic: Poison may strike yet halberds wound him still."

sentences.zh: 」及駿居內府，以戟為衛焉。

translations.literal: " When Jun dwelt within inner treasury; took halberds as guards.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun later guarded himself with halberds—exactly as warned.

sentences.zh: 永甯初，詔曰：「舅氏失道，宗族隕墜，渭陽之思，孔懷感傷。

translations.literal: Early Yongning, edict stated, "Maternal clan lost way; lineage clan fell and crashed; Wei-yang's longing; very bosom feels wounded.
translations.idiomatic: An Yongning edict read: "The Yang clan fell—We grieve for maternal kin."

sentences.zh: 其以{艸務}亭侯楊超為奉朝請、騎都尉，以慰《蓼莪》之思焉。」

translations.literal: Let village marquis Mao ting Yang Chao be Court Presenter, Commandant of Cavalry, to console thoughts of "Deer Veitch's Cry.""
translations.idiomatic: Appoint Mao village marquis Yang Chao as court presenter and cavalry commandant to honor mourning rites described in the ode "Deer Veitch's Cry.""

sentences.zh: 珧字文琚，歷位尚書令、衛將軍。

translations.literal: Yao's courtesy name Wenju; served as Director of the Masters of Writing, General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yao (courtesy Wenju) rose to director of the Masters of Writing and general who guards the army.

sentences.zh: 素有名稱，得幸于武帝，時望在駿前。

translations.literal: Long had reputation and reputation; obtained favor from Emperor Wu; contemporary esteem before Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Once favored above Jun by Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 以兄貴盛，知權寵不可居，自乞遜位，前後懇至，終不獲許。

translations.literal: Because elder brother noble and flourishing; knew power favor could not dwell; self-requested yielding position; front and back earnest to utmost; to end did not obtain permission.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his brother's excess he begged to resign—always refused.

sentences.zh: 初，聘後，珧表曰：「曆觀古今，一族二後，未嘗以全，而受覆宗之禍。

translations.literal: Earlier, after empress betrothal, Yao memorialized, saying, "Throughout surveying antiquity and present, one clan two empresses—never thereby whole—instead receiving overturn-clan calamity.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Yang's selection Yao warned: "Two empresses from one clan doom every clan that tries it."

sentences.zh: 乞以表事藏之宗廟，若如臣之言，得以免禍。

translations.literal: Beg to take memorial affair store it ancestral temple; if like your subject's words, obtain thereby escaping calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Archive this memorial in the ancestral shrine—if I am right it may save us."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Followed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 右軍督趙休上書陳：「王莽五公，兄弟相代。

translations.literal: Supervisor of Right Army Zhao Xiu submitted memorial stating: "Wang Mang's five dukes—brothers succeeded each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiu cited Wang Mang's five brother dukes as warning.

sentences.zh: 今楊氏三公，並在大位，而天變屢見，臣竊為陛下憂之。

translations.literal: Now Yang clan three dukes—together in great positions—yet heaven's anomalies repeatedly appear; your subject privately for Your Majesty worries them.
translations.idiomatic: Three Yangs hold power while omens multiply—I fear for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」由此珧益懼。

translations.literal: " From this Yao grew ever more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: " Yao grew terrified.

sentences.zh: 固求遜位，聽之，賜錢百萬、絹五千匹。

translations.literal: Firmly sought yielding position; permitted it; gifted cash million bolts silk five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: This time his resignation stuck—plus a million cash and five thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 珧初以退讓稱，晚乃合朋黨，構出齊王攸。

translations.literal: Yao early by yielding called praised; late then joined faction partisans; framed removing Prince of Qi You.
translations.idiomatic: Once praised for humility, Yao later joined factions that drove Prince Sima You from court.

sentences.zh: 中護軍羊琇與北軍中侯成粲謀欲因見珧而手刃之。

translations.literal: Central Protector Yang Xiu and Central Commandant of Northern Army Cheng Can plotted wishing when seeing Yao to hand-blade him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu and Cheng Can plotted to stab Yao at audience.

sentences.zh: 珧知而辭疾不出。

translations.literal: Yao knew and declined illness not emerging.
translations.idiomatic: Yao feigned illness and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 諷有司奏琇，轉為太僕。

translations.literal: Insinuated relevant offices memorialize Xiu; transferred to Minister Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: He maneuvered Yang Xiu aside as minister coachman.

sentences.zh: 自是舉朝莫敢枝梧，而素論盡矣。

translations.literal: From this entire court none dared resist crosswise; yet plain reputations exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After that no one crossed him—yet his honor died.

sentences.zh: 珧臨刑稱冤，云：「事在石函，可問張華。

translations.literal: Yao facing execution cried injustice, saying, "Affair is in stone casket—can ask Zhang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: At execution Yao protested: "The iron-clad edicts in the stone chest prove my case—ask Zhang Hua."

sentences.zh: 」當時皆謂宜為申理，合依鐘毓事例。

translations.literal: " People of the time all said ought to extend plea for justice; fitting follow Zhong Yu precedent.
translations.idiomatic: " Court opinion favored review per Zhong Yu's precedent.

sentences.zh: 而賈氏族党待諸楊如仇，促行刑者遂斬之。

translations.literal: Yet Jia clan partisans treated various Yangs like enemies; urged executioners then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jia partisans hated the Yangs and rushed the executioner.

sentences.zh: 時人莫不嗟歎焉。

translations.literal: People of the time none did not sigh and lament.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers groaned at the injustice.

sentences.zh: 珧弟濟

translations.literal: Yao's younger brother Ji
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji—Yao's younger brother

sentences.zh: 濟字文通，歷位鎮南、征北將軍，遷太子太傅。

translations.literal: Ji's courtesy name Wentong; served as General Who Guards the South, General Who Conquers the North; transferred Grand Tutor to Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji (courtesy Wentong) commanded southern and northern armies before becoming grand tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 濟有才藝，嘗從武帝校獵北芒下，與侍中王濟俱著布袴褶，騎馬執角弓在輦前。

translations.literal: Ji had talent and arts; once followed Emperor Wu reviewing hunt beneath Northern Mang; together with Palace Attendant Wang Ji both wore cloth trousers pleats; rode horses grasping horn bows before imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted and athletic, he once rode beside Wang Ji in hunting dress before Emperor Wu's chariot at Mang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 猛獸突出，帝命王濟射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Fierce beast burst forth; Emperor ordered Wang Ji shoot it; responding to string fell over.
translations.idiomatic: When a beast charged Emperor Wu ordered Wang Ji to shoot it dead.

sentences.zh: 須臾復一出，濟受詔又射殺之，六軍大叫稱快。

translations.literal: Momentarily again one emerged; Ji received edict again shot killed it; Six Armies greatly shouted praising delight.
translations.idiomatic: Another beast followed; Yang Ji killed it on command—the army roared approval.

sentences.zh: 帝重兵官，多授貴戚清望，濟以武藝號為稱職。

translations.literal: Emperor esteemed military officials; many invested noble kin clear reputation; Ji by martial arts styled fitting duty.
translations.idiomatic: While military posts went to well-connected nobles, Yang Ji earned praise as truly capable.

sentences.zh: 與兄珧深慮盛滿，乃與諸甥李斌等共切諫。

translations.literal: Together with elder brother Yao deeply worried excess fullness; thereupon with various nephews-by-marriage Li Bin et al. together earnestly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yao warned Jun against hubris with nephews like Li Bin.

sentences.zh: 駿斥出王佑為河東太守，建立皇儲，皆濟謀也。

translations.literal: Jun expelled Wang You out as Administrator of Hedong; establishing imperial heir—all Ji's stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's posting Wang You to Hedong and settling the heir apparent followed Ji's counsel.

sentences.zh: 初，駿忌大司馬汝南王亮，催使之籓。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jun envied Grand Marshal Prince of Runan Liang; urged making him go to fief.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had pressed Grand Marshal Sima Liang toward his fief.

sentences.zh: 濟與斌數諫止之，駿遂疏濟。

translations.literal: Ji together with Bin repeatedly remonstrated stopping him; Jun thereupon estranged Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Li Bin protested until Jun turned against Ji.

sentences.zh: 濟謂傅咸曰：「若家兄征大司馬入，退身避之，門戶可得免耳。

translations.literal: Ji said to Fu Xian, "If elder brother of family summons Grand Marshal to enter, withdraw body avoiding him—household gates can obtain escape only.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji told Fu Xian: "If my brother recalls Grand Marshal Sima Liang to court and we step aside, our kin might survive."

sentences.zh: 不爾，行當赤族。

translations.literal: If not thus, proceeding will face red clan.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise we face total extermination."

sentences.zh: 」咸曰：「但征還，共崇至公，便立太平，無為避也。

translations.literal: " Xian said, "Only summon back; together venerate utmost fairness—then establish great peace—need not avoid.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Xian replied: "Recall Liang to share power openly and peace follows—no retreat needed."

sentences.zh: 夫人臣不可有專，豈獨外戚！

translations.literal: As for ministers not permitted monopoly—how only maternal kin!
translations.idiomatic: Ministers must not monopolize authority—why blame only in-laws!"

sentences.zh: 今宗室疏，因外戚之親以得安，外戚危，倚宗室之重以為援，所謂脣齒相依，計之善者。

translations.literal: Now imperial clan is distant; relying on maternal kin's closeness thereby obtains peace; maternal kin endangered—lean on imperial clan's weight as aid—so-called lips and teeth mutually depend—planning's good course.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial house and empress's clan are lip and teeth—each needs the other; that is wise policy."

sentences.zh: 」濟益懼而問石崇曰：「人心云何？

translations.literal: " Ji grew ever more fearful and asked Shi Chong, saying, "Men's hearts—how are they?
translations.idiomatic: " Growing desperate Yang Ji asked Shi Chong what men thought of the regime."

sentences.zh: 」崇曰：「賢兄執政，疏外宗室，宜與四海共之。

translations.literal: " Chong said, "Worthy elder brother holds governance; estranges outer imperial clan—ought with four seas share it.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi Chong answered: "Your brother rules yet alienates the Sima princes—share power with the realm."

sentences.zh: 」濟曰：「見兄，可及此。

translations.literal: " Ji said, "Seeing elder brother—can reach this.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Ji said he would urge Jun when they met."

sentences.zh: 」崇見駿，及焉，駿不納。

translations.literal: " Chong saw Jun; arrived there; Jun did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi Chong relayed this to Jun, who ignored it.

sentences.zh: 後與諸兄俱見害。

translations.literal: Later together with elder brothers all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Ji died with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 難發之夕，東宮召濟。

translations.literal: Night when rebellion erupted, Eastern Palace summoned Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern palace summoned Yang Ji on the coup's eve.

sentences.zh: 濟謂裴楷曰：「吾將何之？

translations.literal: Ji said to Pei Kai, "Where shall I go?
translations.idiomatic: He asked Pei Kai where he should go."

sentences.zh: 」楷曰：「子為保傅，當至東宮。

translations.literal: " Kai said, "You are protector-tutor—ought go to Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Pei Kai answered: "You tutor the heir—you must attend the eastern palace."

sentences.zh: 」濟好施，久典兵馬，所從四百餘人皆秦中壯士，射則命中，皆欲救濟。

translations.literal: " Ji loved generosity; long commanded soldiers and horses; followers over four hundred were all Guanzhong stalwarts; shooting then hit target—all wished to rescue Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Generous and long a commander, Yang Ji led four hundred crack bowmen from Qin who wanted to fight for him."

sentences.zh: 濟已入宮，莫不歎恨。

translations.literal: Ji had already entered palace; none did not sigh in regret.
translations.idiomatic: Once he obeyed the summons his men groaned with frustration.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：賈充以諂諛陋質，刀筆常材，幸屬昌辰，濫叨非據。

translations.literal: The historian says: Jia Chong by flattery base substance, knife-brush ordinary timber—luckily belonged to flourishing morning—recklessly presumed improper station.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Jia Chong was a petty flatterer of modest talent who rose only because times were flush—yet he seized offices beyond his worth.

sentences.zh: 抽戈犯順，曾無猜憚之心；

translations.literal: Drew halberd violating obedience—never had suspicious dread heart;
translations.idiomatic: He drew arms against his sovereign without flinching;

sentences.zh: 杖鉞推亡，遽有知難之請，非惟魏朝之悖逆，抑亦晉室之罪人者歟！

translations.literal: Staffing axe pushing destruction—suddenly had knowing-difficulty request—not only Wei's court rebel—also Jin house's criminal person!
translations.idiomatic: brandished command against defeat yet pleaded ignorance when conquest loomed—traitor to Wei and criminal to Jin alike!

sentences.zh: 然猶身極寵光，任兼文武，存荷台衡之寄，沒有從享之榮，可謂無德而祿，殃將及矣。

translations.literal: Yet still body reached utmost favor brilliance; duty combined civil and martial; living bore terrace-weight trust; dying had attendant-sacrifice glory—can be called without virtue yet salary—calamity about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Still he enjoyed supreme favor, civil and military power, regent's burden in life and sacrifice honors in death—rank without virtue invites disaster.

sentences.zh: 逮乎貽厥，乃乞丐之徒，嗣惡稔之餘基，縱奸邪之凶德。

translations.literal: When it came to leaving legacy—then beggar's kind; continuing evil ripe remainder foundation; indulging treacherous vicious virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His heirs were mere adventurers who piled evil higher and unleashed wickedness.

sentences.zh: 煽茲哲婦，索彼惟家，雖及誅夷，曷雲塞責。

translations.literal: Fan this wise-woman; rope that only-house—although reaching execution slaughter—how say block responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: They inflamed that clever woman and devastated the house—execution hardly atoned.

sentences.zh: 昔當塗闕翦，公閭實肆其勞，典午分崩，南風亦盡其力，可謂「君以此始，必以此終」，信乎其然矣。

translations.literal: Formerly at Tu-road Wei pruning—Gonglü truly deployed his labor; Overseeing Horse split apart—South Wind also exhausted strength—can be called "lord by this begins, must by this end"—trustworthy how thus!
translations.idiomatic: He labored to topple Wei and helped tear Jin apart—proving "what begins in treason ends in ruin."

sentences.zh: 楊駿階緣寵倖，遂荷棟樑之任，敬之猶恐弗逮，驕奢淫泆，庸可免乎？

translations.literal: Yang Jun stepped via favor intimacy; thereupon bore ridgepole beam duty—revering him still feared not reaching—arrogance extravagance dissipation—how could avoid!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun climbed through palace favor yet mishandled the pillar's burden—revere him he still failed—could arrogance and excess spare him?

sentences.zh: 括母以明智全身，會昆以先言獲宥，文琚識同曩烈，而罰異昔人，裴夫！

translations.literal: Guo's mother by bright wisdom preserved body; Hui's brothers by prior speech obtained mercy; Wenju insight matched former martyrs—yet punishment differed from former men—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Wise mothers and candid brothers survived while Wenju shared earlier heroes' insight yet suffered worse—alas!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：公閭便佞，心乖雅正。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: Gonglü glib flattery—heart deviates from upright correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Jia Chong flattered his way forward with a heart estranged from integrity.

sentences.zh: 邀遇時來，遂階榮命。

translations.literal: Intercept meeting time's arrival—thereupon stepped to glorious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune lifted him to undeserved honors.

sentences.zh: 乞丐承緒，凶家亂政。

translations.literal: Beggars inherit threads—ominous house disorders governance.
translations.idiomatic: His heirs—upstarts—ruined house and state.

sentences.zh: 瑣瑣文長，遂居棟樑。

translations.literal: Petty petty Wenzhang—thereupon dwelt ridgepole beam.
translations.idiomatic: Petty Yang Jun nonetheless bore the state's beam.

sentences.zh: 據非其位，乃底滅亡。

translations.literal: Occupying not his position—thereupon reached extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Usurping rank he marched to ruin.

sentences.zh: 珧雖先覺，亦罹禍殃。

translations.literal: Yao although foresaw—also suffered calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Even foresight could not spare Yang Yao.
